review: The seats on the way to Cancun from Mexico City were cramped, and the layout for all the seats was the same - first class and economy were no different. Checking in online from Cancun to Mexico City was a nightmare. First of all, you need the app and to register for their points program to check-in online. After that they gave my wife and me middle seats in different rows (I didn't pay for specific seats). Then I tried to change our seats and had to pay for "comfort" seats (same as economy but further forward) and was bombarded with attempts to sell me First Class seats (same as economy but further forward). When I paid for the "comfort" seats the payment "failed" for unknown reasons and so I tried again and the exact same seats were over double the price! The price increased by over double as soon as my payment "failed" for unknown reasons, and the comfort seats were now more expensive than the upgrade to First Class! Scammers! We'll just sit in different rows to Mexico City.

Seats are hard as a rock, slanting downwards, permanent butt formations, but have extendable height and wrap around head rests. LCD screen is not user friendly. Seats seem to be wide enough for most passengers. Seat reclines. Aisle requires people to walk sideways to navigate. Insufficient storage, many bags had to be checked at gate.

We had a trip to Dublin from Orlando Fl from 09/21/2022 to 09/29/22 (direct flights). It took me 5 different phone calls (due to excessive wait times) to get seat assignments with extra legroom, but finally secured them. On our outbound flight, the seats were not worth the extra cost - I'm 5'4" tall and my knees were hitting the seat in front me. So little room that you can't even bend down to get your bag from under the seat in front of you. When we arrived in Dublin we discovered that my husbands bag never made the flight - we had checked in 2 1/2 hours before the flight. He did not receive his bag until Tuesday - our flight was on the previous Thursday/arriving Friday morning - that's four days. Their online baggage claim portal site that is supposed to keep you updated on the status of your bag was never once updated - again multiple phone calls had to be made. The fun wasn't over yet, our return flight on the 29th was cancelled. This was due to the hurricane in Florida, so we didn't blame the airline at all, but what we did have a problem with is that we never received a single email or notification of this - I checked the flight status on their website. We were automatically rebooked on a flight from Dublin to London, but with no way of getting from London to Orlando. Again, we had to call them to make the changes. We were rebooked on a flight from Dublin to Newark to Orlando (this leg was on United airlines because Aer Lingus could not accommodate us). On the 7 1/2 hour flight from Dublin to Newark we were given even worse seats than the flight over, less legroom if you can believe it, and the seats did not recline the whole cursory 3/4 of an inch normally allowed. Long story short, this airline needs to get its act together, and airlines as a whole need to be regulated for the amount of space to be provided to economy class passengers. Not everyone can afford the extra $1000+ for business class seats.

The aircraft looked very old from its interiors. The legroom was good for economy class. The seat was old, the screen was not working, tray table was in bad shape, I virtually had to hold it with one hand while having meals with the other. The charging slot was broken. Screen was not working.

2 seats were allocated to me & my wife in the new A350 where both seats were not reclining. The ground staff was unaware & did nothing to sort the issue. Similarly on my flight from Delhi to Sydney on 11 May24, one seat had the same reclining issue. Air India management needs to have a good look to improve its reputation on customer services ... sorry state of affairs...

Seat looked comfortable but was not in fact. The colours were the typical Air India arrangement two peach/orange at window and aisle and one red in the middle. The recline was ok for the aircraft type but the cushion at back was all gone, it was almost hard plane surface, felt like sitting on a wooden chair. legroom was acceptable if not comfortable. width was not a problem for me as I am not too wide. seat base though was comfortable. No charging point was there, neither plugs nor USB, but was not a problem for a flight of little over an hour. TV screen was not available

The cramped leg space left many passengers uncomfortable, and despite the efforts of the flight crew, the situation remained unaddressed. The seats were not comfortable for long-distance travel, resulting in jammed knees and severe pain.

Seats are broken, they squeak when you relax and annoying. Imagine sleeping in an environment where snoring, squeaking continuously going on and flight duration is 14 hours or so. Dirt is all around with broken or non functional TV monitors, remote wire pulled stuck and doesn’t retract. Seats are not comfortable for heavy person like me. Call for attendant it stays lit and No one bothers to show up.

Very poor experience flying with Air India. Most passengers in Economy Class had something wrong with their seat. In my row, on both my departing and returning flights, none of the three seats had a working screen. My seat did not recline either time. On my departing flight, my seat was missing it's bottom cushion, so I was sitting on a thin layer of padding over hard plastic. The food was very terrible. Given that it's Air India, they have a very limited number of non-vegetarian meals even though most of the passengers were non-vegetarian. So during all meals they were out of non-veg meals by the time they got to me. I generally like vegetarian food, but the food they served was honestly so terrible.

Worst aircraft. The seat didn’t recline as the button didn’t seem to work. The inflight screen didn’t work as the touchscreen plus the controls were broken. We spent 8 hours of the flight staring at the air India logo on the screen. USB broken so couldn’t charge our phones either. Never flying Air India again.

I flew Toronto to Delhi on Jan 19, 2023 and Returned on Feb 15, 2023. On both the flights my seat was changed at the time of Boarding. Seat deficiency was sited as a reason. The seats assigned to me on January 19 was 14A . This seat did not work as it could not be straightened and I got the worst hip pain at this seat. The hostess offered me another seat, which could not be reclined and had to change from one to the other. Very uncomfortable. The seat assigned to me on Feb 15 was 12A. This seat minimally straightened and reclined. The TV remote was stuck. could not use it even after cold boot of the system. Having spent a significant amount of money for this travel, the comfort was missing on both the flights and my major concern was my hip getting strained.

Horrible experience, I have paid for the extra leg room seat and the seats in aircraft was disgusting and very uncomfortable. It was not pushing back or once it's pushed back it was not staying still. In 4 of the booked seats, 3 of the seats with broken entertainment screens. Travelled multiple times with multiple airlines but this was an worse experience. Compare to any other airlines cost of tickets was nearly similar.

I was seated in exit row in the economy class cabin. The seat was perhaps the worst I have ever had the privilege of using. The seat was torn, dirty and shabby with absolutely no storage space of any kind. The head rest had lost its shape and the cushioning was worn out, the tray table barely holding together and the backrest was in a weird angle which made it impossible to find a comfortable seating position. The best part was that the IFE remote is big and bulges into the seat making the narrow seat even more painful since it digs painfully into your hip all the time and just because you have a remote doesn't mean that it works since IFE was not operating on almost all seats of the aircraft due to the ancient monitors which must have been broken. The 15 hour journey on this seat from Delhi to Chicago was an epic nightmare. The only good part was the ample legroom since this seat was right next to the lavatory.

The seats were firm and were hard to have a good sleep on (I was able to too because of the 2 AM departure time). While the seats are said to be lie-flat, I don't think they were and it was hard to sleep in the complete "lie-flat" position. A blanket was provided but I had to ask for a pillow on the flight. The sets of 3 on the last 2 rows are reserved for cabin crew to use as rest-areas which reduces the amount of noise around your seats if seated there and also increases privacy. The seat was the longest or widest making it hard to stretch out or sleep in a fetal position. You will have to step over your neighbour if they happen to be in a lie-flat position which can be painful at times. A snack bag was provided as were 2 hot meals, all of which tasted pretty good. The IFE screen lagged a lot and there were barely any options to watch on the IFE screen (I recommend carrying your own entertainment devices) and the headphones were terrible (Recommend carrying your own) Wouldn't recommend this flight unless there ae no other suitable options.

A fairly typical layout for business class on a Boeing 787. The seats are made of fabric and are comfortable. You can adjust the firmness of the seat and there is a massage feature (fairly basic though). One sandwich was provided on the 1.5-hour flight from Hyderabad to Delhi which is reasonable considering the duration of the flight and the fact this trip was during the COVID pandemic. The seat was comfortable and wide enough for me to expect a good sleep, a minor inconvenience would be having to step over your neighbour if you happen to have one. All in all, a nice flight

These are new seats and really comfortable. I had a window seat which faces slightly towards the window which was nice for the views and also it faces away from everyone else. The monitor is quite large and touch screen and has a remote by the side of the seat. The seat can turn flat when i am sleeping and was really comfortable. There was lots of storage which was great and sockets for power.

The seats on the Air China Boeing 747-400 are well padded but does not include personal inflight entertainment system. There is a overhead inflight entertainment system.  For 5’6 me, I am able to stretch my feet without touching the seat in front. There is a foot rest. The tray table is spacious.However they can improve on their recline as my seat only reclined one or two inches. Other than that the seat was wonderful.

AC633 on 6 January 2026, our assigned seats were 19H and 19J, originally intended for my 13‑year‑old daughter and 6‑year‑old son. Shortly after takeoff, water began leaking onto these seats. I reported the issue to the flight attendants, who told me it was “normal due to condensation.” Despite this explanation, the leak continued throughout the flight, with water dripping onto us and soaking our clothes. This made the journey extremely uncomfortable, especially for children. The only assistance offered was a napkin, which was clearly inadequate for an ongoing leak. No one followed up, offered alternative seating, or showed concern for the discomfort and wellbeing of my children or myself. For a long‑haul international flight, this level of service and care is unacceptable.

Seats very narrow. There is not much arm or leg space, even for someone who are small. I selected 42A for outbound and 42K for inbound, both are window seats, close but not next to the lavatory. Can't say it is a good choice. Had to cross two people to get out of my seats. Both of them have to stand up at the aisle in order for me to get out. Any movement will Also, it's hard to recline the back of seat. Entertainment system is good, good selection of shows to watch.

Air Canada has the worst economy seat of airlines I have flown. The seat was torturous on this 13.5 hour flight from Dubai to Toronto. The seats have a light construction with poor cushioning and a terrible lumbar support. The adjustable head rest was very uncomfortable. The seat material was abrasive and added to my discomfort. The seats had no front foot rest. While the recline was reasonable and perhaps considerate of passengers behind, some seats reclined more than others.
Seat was the worst that I've seen on a long flight. Hard and uncomfortable seats that recline poorly and terrible legroom. The seat caused me back pain for a long time.

The seats were absolutely terrible in every way. Felt like sitting on concrete. The cushions were poorly attached and slid around when you moved. There was little to no back support. No legroom whatsoever. I literally could not sit with my legs in front of me, and could barely fit my backpack under the seat. Also no power outlet anywhere.

The seating is very cramped and uncomfortable with less legroom particularly for tall individuals. It feels like they are maximising revenues with addition of more seats thereby reducing customer comfort. Worse still the cabin crew is unhelpful and leaves customers fending for themselves. Cabin crew walking in the aisle keep brushing passengers sitting on the aisle seat. The headphone jack sound was not clear, there was loose connection. The display abruptly shut down for a few random seats some time down the flight and took long to restart again. Display was not responding. Cabin storage space was also relatively less. The crew was clueless on what caused the shutdown. The power plug too was slow to charge cellphone.

I flew business class after Covid-19 measures were implemented, so I came in expecting reduced cabin service, and that was what I got. That being said, even with all the precautionary measures, I was surprised that they were still able to put a somewhat decent service together. Air Canada uses Super Diamond seats, which arrange passengers in a reverse herringbone configuration. It's a pretty standard product, though I must say I really like the colour scheme that Air Canada uses. It just looks really clean and the colours contrast nicely. Due COVID-19, I requested the upgrade to business as a precautionary measure, and I wasn't disappointed. Even with reduced cabin services, it was still a nice experience. Sure, there's no pillow or bar service- they've warned about this on their website, but as it turned out, when they said they would be serving pre-packaged meals, all they meant was that they weren't going to plate your meal for you. It was still business quality (veal from Hawksworth), but they simply didn't give you that picture perfect plating that is so greatly appreciated. Despite the lack of a pillow, the seats were still quite comfortable, though it could still do with more lumbar support, and the lack of a pillow made the sleeping position a tad awkward because my head was dipped backwards even with the power adjustable headrest. Service could admittedly be a bit more polished, though to be fair, part of this definitely has to do with the COVID-19 precautions. I should probably try upgrading again when this blows over. I do appreciate how quiet the cabin was, and was pleasantly surprised to see that the food quality was not compromised as a result of their infection control measures.

I picked seat 13A, which is right behind the bulkhead seat. This was a good choice, especially since the bulkhead row does not let you fully stretch your legs outwards, and you also don't get seat storage at all. The seat reclines, and the footrest folds down from the seat in front of you (again, another reason not to take the bulkhead seat). I would note that the Singapore Airlines leg rests for Premium Economy are nicer, since they extend from under your seat. It would be nice if they installed a clip at the end of the tray table, because the second half of it is really flimsy, but on the bright side, these seats were definitely felt newer than the ones they had fitted on their 777-300ERs.

Having recently flown with Aegean Airlines, I found the legroom to be highly disappointing. As depicted in the attached image, the legroom is virtually non-existent. My knees were pressed against the seat in front of me, which made for an incredibly uncomfortable flight experience. When the passenger in front of me reclined their seat, it became impossible to move. This lack of space is a significant inconvenience. There is no improvement in space or comfort as you move towards the back of the plane, making it a consistent problem for a large portion of the cabin.  I would recommend Aegean Airlines to reconsider their seating configuration to enhance passenger comfort.

The new A320neo feels worse than an old A320. The colours give however a nice touch. The seat pitch was awful and actually borderline for someone who’s over 185 cm.  Food was simple and not great. I would strongly avoid changing at Athens airport. Changing planes for a non Schengen destination means leaving the security area and going through security again. This was not communicated beforehand.

Took a flight at 25B on A320neo (SX-NEO) with Aegean's new cabin layout and in short it feels like a downgrade. I am an Aegean frequent flyer (Gold Miles&Bonus). The good: USB (B type) power for all passengers, place to put your phone/tablet in front of you, lighter/fresh cabin colors. The bad: New seat feels claustrophobic as the upper part of the front seat takes more area in front of you, the lower part of front seats seem bulkier now resulting to less legroom space, resulting obstructed access to aisle (you have to walk diagonally and you need to hold onto something). In addition to moving the toilets to the rear end to fit a new seat row, making them also claustrophobic, overall the new cabin is a downgrade.

Seating seemed to be the same as Economy, with the exception that the middle seat was kept empty, and there was more leg room. I found the legroom to be ample and I am fairly tall. Standard recline. Not particularly wide, but I am!  The price was reasonable.
Very good overall, but I'm taller than 6' and seats are very narrow. I find it disgusting to have to pay for extra leg room. Definitely not recommend it for tall people.

Never had less legroom on a flight than during the flight with the new Aegean A320neo. The seat pitch was very narrow, and they allow reclining the seat in economy. So the very limited space gets even smaller if the person in front insists reclining.  Add around 36 Euro on top for "extra legroom" charges for 2 international flights. Or just book somewhere else.

The service was terrific but could not overcome the fact that the business class seat / bed did not function. The flight attendant had to lower it from sitting to fully reclined and back again, there was no in between setting. I was told that 11 of the about 120 seats were out of order. Do Not Fly this airline unless it is coach. Also, it was late taking off all three flights.
Small spaces between the seats. The TVs not working or working poorly. The choices of food is limited, and they don't offer vegetarian options of meals. They just don’t care!
Very uncomfortable seats. Very narrow. No information about the flight on the seat’s screen, only the remaining time until arrival. No free headsets to watch the only 10 films they have available.
One of the most comfortable seats with more than average knee room in economy class. I have travelled economy in varying airlines and I found this to be the best.

We flew from Vancouver to Paris and did not get anything extra other than a bag containing a toothbrush and a few other things compared to economy. We had one meal service and one snack before landing and they did not came around once in between the meal service. Terrible for premium economy.
For long haul flights the seats in economy are unacceptable, especially by paying extra for the 22A.

Avoid Seat 1J on the A350. The only window is non operational with the blind locked closed for whatever reason. As an older traveler who likes to look out of the window in order to focus my eyesight, this was terrible. Considering the cost of this ticket (and very poor crew service today), we shall be changing our future AF flights.

The advantage of the shell type seat is that nobody will recline and hit your knees. However if you are tall, they are not very comfortable for an 11 hour flight. The In-flight entertainment Entertainment System is of very good quality, even on dated 777 aircrafts
Not much to say other than comfortable enough, good legroom and clean, met expectations for short haul and was comfortable for a 2 hour flight not much more to comment on!
Attention it's a plus. They spoil me all the flight. Food was great also wines. The desserts was the best. Full lie flat bed, loved it! The lounge at Paris was just OK. Could be better.

I always have a good experience on Air France flights, especially now that US Airlines have overall dropped so much in quality, but there are small things that keep annoying me. In particular, I keep wondering why is it that they have head sets with two-prong jacks (with one that you have to fold on the side), when the actual jack plug has only one hole (see photo attached). Furthermore, the stereo sound often doesn't work and plays only in one ear (that was the case on my flight last Monday). Does that make any sense at all? On top of that, the USB port below the TV screen was not working, so I could not charge my phone. It's too bad, because I do like AF in general.

A330 Business class product is awful. Was no selection of food and was given a very bland pasta despite having a gluten intolerance. Cabin AC was faulty and stuck on lowest setting. Cabin crew did the best they could. Customer services response was pathetic.

The business class seat had plenty of room, and I liked that it was a pod-style (so I had decent privacy). My biggest complaint is the comfort when in bed mode it is very lumpy with the lumbar protruding into your back.  AF has invested a lot into these seats, and they could be great if they would only take the time to work on them a bit. A lay-flat bed that protrudes into your back is not OK. Tried using an extra blanket to make the bed more comfy but it didn't work. Please Air France, improve the comfort of the cushions for bed mode.

A premium flatbed seat for USD50 over a regular seat needed no convincing. Even though it wasn’t a complete 180° flatbed, it got to about 160° which was still pretty good and decent enough for some rest. I had no issues stretching out completely. Width, length and comfort were all very decent and well worth the upgrade. Pillows and blankets provided too.

Regular business class passengers, we were (once again unfortunately) dealing with a maintenance problem with your equipment, namely your business seats. I had reserved seats 1D and 1E for my wife and myself and we had a very unpleasant surprise because upon boarding we were allocated other seats because the 1E was broken (and had been for several flights!). Initially the person at check-in separated us and at my insistence I was still able to have 2 seats side by side, and we were again moved for the second section towards Paris and this time right next to the WC where a painful flight! If I take the trouble to pay for business class and reserve seats 1D and 1E it is because we are very tall and the space for the feet is more important on these seats while all the others have a ridiculous little triangle for foot rest and it is almost impossible for us to sleep. In short, this is not the first time that I have experienced this type of problem with ATN and it is becoming really problematic. The business seats are in a deplorable state since some are patched up with plaster, others are dislocated (I took many photos of the cabin if you are interested). I had an interview with the purser who sent a message via her on-board iPad but it had no effect. Passagers régulier de la classe poerava business nous avons eu (encore une fois hélas) affaire à un problème d'entretien de votre matériel, à savoir vos sièges business. J'avais réservé pour mon épouse et moi même les fauteuils 1D et 1E et nous avons eu une très mauvaise surprise car dès l'embarquement on nous attribue d'autres sièges car le 1E était cassé (et ce depuis plusieurs vols!). Au départ la personne au check in nous séparait et devant mon insistance j'ai quand même pu avoir 2 sièges cote à cote, et nous avons encore était déplacés pour le second tronçon vers Paris et cette fois juste à coté des WC d'où un vol pénible !. Si je prend la peine de payer une classe business et de réserver les sièges 1D et 1E c'est que nous sommes très grands et l'espace pour les pieds est plus important sus ces sièges tandis que tous les autres ont un petit triangle ridicule pour repose pieds et il nous est quasiment impossible de dormir. Bref, ce n'est pas la première fois que je subis ce genre de problemes avec ATN et cela devient vraiment problématique. Les sièges business sont dans un état lamentables puisque certains sont rafistolés avec du sparadrap, d'autres sont déboités (j'ai fait de nombreuses photos de la cabine si cela vous intéresse). J'ai eu un entretien avec la chef de cabine qui a envoyé un message via son ipad de bord mais cela n'a eu aucun effet.

If you want a seat you have to pay 30euros - we paid 4 seats round trip so 240€. None of our initial seat allocation was respected. The day before flying, they allocated us in the middle of aircraft. They should have informed us and refunded window seats. After calling, we had to go to the airport first to renegotiate our paid seats - my claustrophobic father was really stressed out thinking about not seeing outside. They removed us from our seat to gather a family of 7 people. But they changed all allocation to give what we paid for. On the trip back to Paris, I checked in online and get our paid seats (row 38 - same as 1st flight). I initially asked for those seats to be free to apologize for their first mistake but they never answered. However, we were given boarding passes with row 27 next to toilets instead of 38. I again needed to go and ask to change everything. I complained on the 5th December to get a refund for the seats and I remained 84 days without any answer. They guarantee and answer within 72h. On departure day, I did not sleep all night because my father was scared (first time he flew) - we had to go to the airport at 7am instead of 9am as we wanted - so we paid night taxi fare to be early because when i called day before they could change our allocation. On flight return they also change allocation. They will tell you they are able to do it regarding their safety policy etc, but on the full flight our seats are not located at emergency exit so no safety reason. To conclude : do not pay any seat because you will start dreaming about Polynesia but it will start and end by a nightmare with seat allocations. Luckily food and flight attendants were great. Booking and reservation and leaders for seats allocation need to be trained. I have never seen a company changing seats allocation. I know 5 other people who faced same issue, and I read here that i am not the only one.

Normally with Allegiant we pay the upcharge for the extra legroom seats, but due to a recent Covid exposure we had to modify our travel dates and there were no extra legroom seats available. So we got stuck in standard seats, my wife in a window seat and me in an aisle. My wife is 6 feet tall with a 32 inch inseam, and I'm 6 foot 2 with a 30 inch inseam. The legroom was miserable. I can't imagine anyone with an even longer leg length shoe-horning into these seats. Hard to believe the FAA permits such small spacing, or that people will loyally fly in such seats. In future I shall only book extra legroom seats with Allegiant - or will fly other airlines. Otherwise I have no problem with Allegiant's business model and approach. But this is a showstopper for us.

Recently flew with Air Transat from London to Toronto, and it was one of the worst flight experiences of my life. Flight attendants totally inattentive. I sat next to the aisle and my shoulder was hit hard over 10 times by the flight attendants without so much as an "Excuse me" or "Sorry".  The headphone jack on the entertainment system was broken so could not use the system to watch movies. No individual air valves to control temperature at your seat so I was cooking on board the flight.The tray table was broken so when the flight attendant put the meal on the table, it slid off into my lap.  Called Air Transat to help resolve the issue, I asked to give us 1 free checked bag on the return leg home to compensate for this ordeal and the answer was no.
Extremely narrow seats, and not very comfortable in terms of reclining, tray size and placement, and seat cushioning. The leg room was decent.

Seats A & C in row 2 Club Class. Flew from Montreal to Rome in the Club Class and worth every dollar. Had issues getting out at night with row in front reclined and people sleeping. Flew home in row 6 seats A & B. Wished all the way home on this 8 hour day time flight that we had splurged on a Club Class seating again. The economy seating was very small and the cushion was maybe 1 inch thick. The attendants were very good and polite.

Being a normal sized guy...5'9" and 165lbs., I was reasonably comfortable on board the 2 flights, both in the 4 hour range. Seats were what I get on most commercial flights I have taken over the past decade. I had 7H (aisle) on the way up and 14c (aisle) on the return. 14c is a great seat and I will book that again! Personally, no complaints from a seasoned flyer.

Online booking and check in was easy but having flown numerous times previously from Gatwick to Toronto and Air Transat has gone downhill. It seems the seat area is smaller equivalent to Easyjet in the UK. I'm 5ft 10" medium build and struggled.. Anyone overweight will not only be extremely uncomfortable but make other passengers suffer. Is the 3x3x3 seating normal on a 330 Airbus? The food was pretty awful. Ok so it's a budget airline and costs are tight, l get that but don't expect much and you're be fine. Just not as it was.

This was by far the most uncomfortable flight. Seats are incredibly hard and way too narrow for any comfort. I had booked an aisle and my boyfriend had the window seat. Most of the time, nobody will take the middle, unless the flight is at capacity. Unfortunately, this time I was asked to move into the middle seat and was sandwiched between two very large men whose shoulders far exceeded the width of the seat, including my own. I am also not a tiny person. I had to sit wedged sideways just to fit and dislocated a rib in the process. I used to enjoy flying with Air Transat, but this has gotten way out of hand. It is truly appalling and cruel to treat people this way. There are only 12 club class on this airline so 12 people can pay an exorbitant amount to be comfortable while the other 300+ passengers get to travel in extreme discomfort.

The seats were horrible! For an 11 hour flight, you'd think the airline would provide an aircraft that's comfortable. The seats were narrow, very little cushion and uncomfortable. We even paid an additional $83 each to upgrade to premium seats. What a waste of money. Pay a little more and fly in comfort, especially when flying overseas or for such a long period of time.

This is the second flight with Air Transat in the last 2 months. Although these planes are newer, the seat comfort is quite terrible. Anyone dealing with any back issues or lower back problems, please re-think this airline. My second flight confirmed why I should avoid Air Transat. It's not worth the cost of the pain, massages and possible chiropractor you will need to recover from these seats. I was on a 5 hour flight - and 4 days later I am still dealing with the pain of those seats.

Toronto to Cancun. Business Class on this leisure airline is known as "Club Class". We enjoyed a most pleasant flight, we began with pre-flight mimosas, our pre-ordered Gourmet meals were good, the IFE performed perfectly (once you get the hang of the pullout control unit, but the also touchscreen works, if you can reach it, it's a Row 1 issue) As compared to years prior, the included Comfort Kits no longer have slippers, so take your past ones, nor headphones which is good as many pax like myself bring our own. The only thing is that by using the second door (around Row 10) to deplane, the crew should make the Economy wait until the Club pax have exited first. Otherwise, for everything you get with AT Club Class, highly recommended.

Gate crew at JFK Terminal 7 Alaska Airlines were of such a degree of incompetence despite ; would not allow us to take on one carry on + one personal item each because of the excuse "no room". After we got on the aircraft, it turns out there was loads of room - they are simply bad at counting. Then told us we still weren't allowed to take the luggage on because the "bag had already been tagged". Aircraft itself has no screen for entertainment even in business class. You have to bring your own laptop to pass the time to the 6 hour flight. Business class gets food; all other classes get nothing.

I have flown on Alaska Airlines for many years. My experience has been usually positive. Good Food, sometimes excellent. On my latest trip from MCO-PDX the food was excellent and service was attentive, and professional. I'm 6'3" and Alaska by far has the most legroom and recline of all, except Trans-con Business/First on Delta, American, United and Jetblue lie flat seats. Portland is a hub airport. I can usually travel to any significant U.S city non-stop and 1 stop to any European City.

This was an amazing seat. Better than delta! I flew from Seattle to Atlanta, and the seat was so wide. I was very impressed, especially for premium and economy. It also reclined with pretty decent reclining. However, there was no seat back entertainment. But that’s ok. I used my iPad. It was free. So yeah! Great experience. For good seats, I definitely recommend Alaska Airlines.

I took a flight from Seoul to Singapore. I paid $56 SGD to select a seat with extra legroom. I chose 10A (window), but on check-in, they told me 10D was better because 10B/C were filled, while 10E/F were empty, so I could have the entire row to myself. What I did not count upon was that my extra leg room because a short-circuit for more than a dozen people to switch from the left aisle to the right aisle so that they could use the right aisle toilet, which was visible, while the left aisle toilet was blocked off by a curtain. This group included one guy shouting at me because my legs were in the way as they traversed the space in front of 10D/E/F. Food was ordinary. Movie was good. Staff were pleasant. If I'd been in seat 10A, I would have enjoyed the flight.

Wasn’t impressed with this flight at all - no air vents above the seat, and cabin temperature fluctuated between 23/25 degrees throughout the whole flight on both legs from LHR - SYD. The purser wouldn’t adjust the cabin temperature as she stated that other passengers were cold, so had to provide me with a fan. Seat was really uncomfortable as a bed, and didn’t find the basic adjustments to the seat formation comfortable at all. Meal options were ok but very rigid - if you didn’t like an aspect of your menu selection, there were no alternatives. Staff were friendly and tried their best to be helpful.

Seat 16A on PSA Airlines’ CRJ-900 is an excellent choice, especially for a short flight like DCA to PHL. Positioned by one of the emergency exit windows, it offers plenty of legroom, making it one of the roomier seats on the aircraft. After a quick and straightforward briefing from the flight attendant—where I agreed to assist in the unlikely event of an emergency—we were on our way. While PSA’s CRJ aircraft are slightly smaller than those operated by other regional carriers in the same market, they are well-suited for the short hops PSA primarily flies. The seat itself was extremely comfortable, and for a 27-minute flight, I couldn’t ask for more. A solid choice for anyone looking for a bit of extra space on a quick journey.

I recently flew American Eagle from DCA to PHL on Republic Airways, and I was particularly impressed with the main economy extra cabin on the E175. The seat design offers an exceptional level of comfort with plush cushioning and enhanced legroom, ensuring a surprisingly pleasant experience on the short 27-minute flight. The thoughtful ergonomic design of the chair made it easy to relax, even on a brief journey. Overall, a well-executed seating configuration that complements Republic Airways commitment to professionalism and efficiency.

The Embraer 175 is, without a doubt, a game-changer for regional travel. The first-class seat, designed for flights of up to 4.5 hours, offers unmatched comfort on shorter routes like the quick 27-minute hop from DCA to PHL. With ample legroom, supportive cushioning, and a well-thought-out design, there’s nothing to complain about, especially on flights averaging under an hour. It’s always surprising when infrequent travelers nitpick a product that delivers exactly what it promises. Republic Airways continues to provide a consistently solid experience for the American Airlines Group, reinforcing why the E175 remains the gold standard for regional flying.

Flying American Eagle on Republic Airlines’ Embraer E175 is a game changer compared to other models. The spacious 2-2 seating in Economy means no middle seats, and First Class offers a private 1-2 layout perfect for solo travelers. The larger overhead bins fit standard carry-ons, so there’s less gate checking hassle. Plus, the bigger windows and ergonomic seats make for a more comfortable ride. Another major perk?… The E175 has two bathrooms, unlike some smaller regional aircraft that only have one in the back making the E175 more convenient for passengers. Given Republic’s excellent service and commitment to passenger comfort, American Airlines should seriously consider bringing them into their group of wholly owned carriers. Their operation stands out, and integrating them could further strengthen the American Eagle brand.

First class seat in the aisle out of the galley and aircraft entrance that sits too close to the bulkhead to stretch legs. During boarding people keep bumping on you and you have to watch your legs every time flight attendants come in and out of the galley. Worst seat of the entire 1st class cabin. Recline is OK for regional 1st class service.

This seat is beyond bad. This is a regional jet, so no IFE or WiFi is no biggie, and being tight is expected. It just shouldn’t be this tight. I’m only 5’8 and about 175 pounds and I had a hard time fitting into the worn and tired seat. One note, this is a Piedmont Aircraft operating as American Eagle.

Pretty standard business class offering with just 3 rows in business. Rock hard seat with middle seat kept free. Reasonable leg room. The flight is short but I wouldn't want this seat if flying for much longer. The plane - OE-LZO is only 5 weeks old so it is still spangly and new. USB A&C for each seat. The flight was a 6am LHR-VIE so breakfast was served. I didn't much like the blueberry cake thing, but the meat/cheese/tomato combo was decent. Croissants and rolls were offered. Excellent coffee. Overall, not bad but could be better.
Definitely the worst flights ever in Economy class. Uncomfortable seats poor seat pitch and recline. If you're taller than 175cm choose another carrier or be ready to be cramped!!!

I travel a lot and this was the worst experience on any long haul flight in economy ever. 10 seats in a row on a 777 and a very low seat pitch resulted in extremely uncomfortable a flight despite fair service and a huge PTV.
Completely unacceptable for a long-haul flight. Seats do not recline much and the ulphostery is very old.
Definitely the worst flights ever in Economy class. Uncomfortable seats poor seat pitch and recline. If you're taller than 175cm choose another carrier or be ready to be cramped!!!

I travel a lot and this was the worst experience on any long haul flight in economy ever. 10 seats in a row on a 777 and a very low seat pitch resulted in extremely uncomfortable a flight despite fair service and a huge PTV.
Completely unacceptable for a long-haul flight. Seats do not recline much and the ulphostery is very old.

Nice seat with a lots of leg room, you can stretch your legs without any problems, maybe a little narrow if in the middle Seat. Normal storage in seat pockets and usb entry. Screen good size but terrible sound.

A burlap sack full of field rocks would be a better seating experience. I have tried both the regular and plus seats in economy and both are absolutely abysmal, both for comfort and space. A true sardines in a crushed tin can experience.
Flight was over 6 hours, seats did not recline and I have never been more uncomfortable in my life. I have seen this for small commuter flights, not long ones like this. Just horrid

Extremely short legroom, very uncomfortable chairs, even with a higher rate what you get is just the chair reclines, not suitable for tall people or long flights. Alsoo in two different trips the flight had delays in departure, the first one of an hour and the next flight more than 3 hours

Seats are so uncomfortable, you have a very little legroom space, seats do not recline and one of the planes I travelled did not have USB port. In a 6 hour flight, New York to Bogota, the plane did not have screens but did have a website for entertainment but it’s not the same. They did not offer a glass of water for free, you had to pay for everything. Do not fly with Avianca on international flights, it’s so uncomfortable.
Seats are extremely uncomfortable, too hard and it’s impossible to be in one position over an hour, which makes it impossible to sleep. Not a good option for an overnight flight.

Hanoi to Ho Chi Minh on a Boeing 787-9. This is a new airline, so I didn’t expect too much on the service. But I love how generous the cabin crew are. I enjoyed the sandwich and the price was so cheap.

It was an older Airbus A320 aircraft, but there were no issues and the hygiene was good. There wasn't a lot of space for my legs (186cm), but ok. But I need to say I had more space at an A320 aircraft from Vueling than with Brussels Airlines. The crew speaks fluently Dutch, French and English and will try help you if you have a question.

Seats are better than what would be expected of a 42 seater aircraft. sufficient legroom, width and recline. nice, clean and soft. my seat was positioned and aligned with the window for a perfect view of mountains and terrains we were flying over and beside. 5A was where I was seating on. sufficient space in the overhead cabin. Overall very good.

This is the worst economy seating I have been on,  the seats are very narrow and the seating hard. Having the back upright feels like you are being pushed froward, in recline they are just about tolerable. The leg room is very tight that cannot move your feet. There is no arm room and if you are in an aisle seat you are constantly being knocked by passengers and crew as they pass. The earphone socket was broken i had an 8hr flight with no entertainment.

BA used a configuration of 2x3x2 seats per row. I was seated in a middle, small, claustrophobic cabin in the middle with no air flow. Service was handled over a passenger seating on both sides and stepping to the aisle required jumping over another passenger.

The business class of British Airways flying London to LA is very poor by comparison to other airlines, for the price. The seating is narrow, on top of a neighbor, no separate little cabin. It's also generally more expensive and the Avios are not worth collecting as there is rarely any availability.

Was sat on that famous row 35, seat 35H. Summary: 11.5 hours flight from LHR to GIG in seat that doesn't recline by default. The seats on the row 34 ahead recline, meaning it's a struggle for eating or drinking if passengers sat on row 34 keep their seats reclined. To make the disaster worse, the overhead bin compartment above rows 33 to 35 are occupied by cabin crew stuff. Means that it is extremely difficult to accommodate cabin luggage.

Recently flew BA’s nonstop between Boston and London on the A380. It is a massive airplane with a payload of over 500 passengers. Business class seating on this plane and on this route was not worth the $$ in my opinion. There were too many seats in each row making the seats narrower than those offered by other airlines. Most jumbo jets have a 1-2-1 configuration in business class; this plane had 2-3-2 and 2-4-2, twice as many seats in each row. This is particularly obnoxious if you are seated in the middle aisle because that means anyone seated in a window seat or in the middle seats has to crawl over an aisle passenger just to get to the bathroom and back. If you do so in the dark on an overnight flight, it is actually unsafe for you and that poor aisle passenger. Check the plane scheduled for the flight you want to take and if a 777 is offered, opt for that one. They are all equipped with Club Suites in Business now.

Sat in seats 24a outbound to Budapest and 18A return flight from Bucharest. Seats were both very worn and had a ridge running a couple of inches from the rear. My backside was numb on both flights and less than 3 hours for each flight. Legroom far to little for a national carrier. Also on the return flight the seat pocket had a hole at the bottom and only found this out when i put items in it and they fell on the floor and due to the lack of space had to ask fellow passengers if they could reach my stuff which they kindly did. USB charger  going very intermittent as well. I will avoid British Airways on short haul flights if possible.
One of the worst business class seats, tiny seat. The lay out of the aircraft is very cramped, the plane was very dirty, amenity kit awful, service in general, not so good.

BA doesn't seem to understand why its customers choose to fly with them over low-cost carriers like Ryanair, easyJet or Wizz Air and the keep racing to the bottom, despite never being cheap enough or comprehensive enough in terms of flights to certain destinations. They've installed the same appalling slimline seats easyJet and Wizz Air have, but managed to make them even more uncomfortable. They have no lumbar support, and also don't have headrests like BA's old Pinnacle seats. They also have no recline and despite being refurbished had no at seat charging either. My understanding was that seats upto row 12 should have the old Pinnacle seats, so I woke up early to check-in just as check-in opened on the app 24hrs before and was pleased to bag a seat in row 10 which should mean I have the old Pinnacle seat. Apparently not, at least not on BA Euroflyer their subsidiary at Gatwick, the whole plane had the new appalling slimline seats even in Business - I'd have been pretty appalled if I had paid extra to fly in that cabin and been left with that seat for 3hrs. They are probably ok for an 1 maybe 2hr flight max, but on a 3hr flight to Catania from Heathrow it was painful and we were left with a horrible back pain.

Boeing 787-9 - not worth the money. The seats were extremely narrow so like lying in a coffin. When the seats were out (which is all the time on these long flights) you have to clamber over passengers to get to the toilet. The configuration of the cabin means that some one is always waking up someone else. This is an economy seat masquerading as a business class seat and is misleading and deceptive conduct because there is NO WAY you can get any rest if you book with British Airways.
Worst seat we have ever had to endure on a long haul flight. No room at all and not what we expected would not recommend this airline

Did research, premium economy, looks good with extra width seats more legroom and extra recline on the seats. We had a 20 hour red eye flight LHR to SYD with a refuelling and quick crew change in SIN. Looks deceive. We were seated in row E (middle 2 of 4) centre aisle. Great, until the seat in front reclined and we discovered we were trapped. The seat arms are not retractable, (that is where the tray table is located). The distance between the arm rest and the fully reclined seat in front is under 7 inches. To extract yourself you have to wake 3 passengers, 2 in front to lift their seat backs to an upright position and the passenger to your side to allow you to lift your legs up over the arm rests. I found it impossible to watch my screen due to it being so far off vertical, it was sending me dizzy looking at it. One other problem I discovered, because I was stressed at being uncomfortable I started getting hot to find the Boeing 777 does not have individual air conditioning cold air nozzles, once the temperature is set it can’t be individually cooled. On the positive side the food was good I did however miss the coffee pot after the meal.

The most uncomfortable flight I have experienced due to the metal boxes under the seat in front. Outbound chose a window seat on lower deck and had one metal box under my seat that made sitting straight very difficult, so on way home opted for an upper deck seat in a set of two with my husband so I could at least get up and stretch. There was two boxes this time, and had pins and needles in my legs for not only the entire flight but for several hours afterwards. As vegan flyers we are never wowed with food, but this one was the worst yet, plain rice and vegetables.

Was sat in the emergency exit row. Ample leg room but was a little tight with elbow room. Entertainment system was ok but would prefer a newer movie selection. Breakfast meal was a little heavy, but enjoyed the selection including fruit, yogurt and croissant. Service professional and courteous. Overall the flight was enjoyable

The seat is quite comfortable and has good legroom, there is good space on the window seats, the IFE is outdated though and you can't adjust the angle of the head rest. The window is very big and your receive some sort of service every 1-2 hrs.

This flight was as I had experienced with all other BA flights I've had. The seats are comfortable, the bedding provided is pretty good, the food on-board (I always order an Asian Vegetarian Meal) was brilliant and the cabin crew brilliant. I sat on one of the window seats (rear-facing) and the privacy you get with the privacy divider up is pretty good. I always select the window seat on the last seat of the cabin (3A on this flight) to prevent having to step over someone else. The only possible criticism I can find for the set is the lack of storage space and how inconveniently placed the one storage bin is. BA is pretty good otherwise.

Was disappointed at first to see I was on the Boeing 777-200 but realised it was the updated club suite cabin so wasn't sad for long. The 1-2-1 configuration is a step up from their 2-3/4-2 configuration and the privacy on the seats is pretty good. The door isn't helpful and is more of a gimmick (could've been higher). The new IFE screens are way better than the older ones, they are more clear and bright and responsive than the old IFE screens. The seats on club suite are still fabric, which in my opinion, is better than leather and more comfortable. The seats now have convenient storage bins and power ports which is a very big improvement when compared to the old club world. The seats also have adjustable armrests which make sliding out of your seat during meal services easy. The service, in general, was fantastic and very similar to other BA flights I've had. All in all club suite is a pretty big improvement over the old business cabin.

All I ask is that BA increase the seat pitch by one inch - one inch would make such a difference; as would a little more padding in the seat and lumber/small of the back region of the seat on this Boeing 777-200.

The smallest leg room I have seen. Customer reclined the seat in front of me is less than 30cm from my face making it impossible to watch a movie as the screen is too close.  Absolutely horrible experience.

We booked Business Class to enjoy a pleasant flight with extended periods of sleep during the flight. We had seats 11D and 11 G, seats that did not have any privacy screen around the seats like the other seats in the Business Class cabin. We got the impression that these seats were added on to maximise the seating in Business Class without any consideration to the comfort of passengers, who paid substantial fees to have the benefits of a Business Class. The seats were adjacent to the two toilets at the front of the cabin, with regular traffic to and from there, with people waiting in the aisle to use the toilets. All the other passengers in the cabin were enclosed and protected by the privacy screens. In addition, the cabin crew made lot of noise in the kitchen area, dropping on numerous occasions metal kitchenware, chatting loudly after lights-out, not respecting our need for a rest. The service was very hectic, we got the impression that the crew had not been trained sufficiently. As far as food was concerned, a number of the items on the cabin menus were not available, or prepared in the kitchen area, as we could witness since most of the time the curtains were not closed. Also, all meals had to be served on hand-held trays carried by the crew through the cabin. This caused extensive delays in serving meals. After several hours of coping with the below-standard seat and service situation, I requested alternative seats from the head stewardess, which she could not provide due to the fact that some business-class seats were already occupied by staff members returning home. So, we were put up in two Premium Economy seats, which provided no opportunity to get any sleep.
9Boeing 777-300 is tatty and needs a refurbishment. The tray table is difficult to remove. On my seat in the premium exit row, the tv screen will not stay in place.

Business Class cabin on the 777–300 (Non-ER, 777-31H) was very dated and disappointing. Stepping into the Business cabin fitted in a 2-3-2 layout, even the most seasoned of frequent fliers would be forgiven for mistaking the cabin for a premium economy cabin. Seats were not lie-flat and could only recline to a 120° angle, touchscreens were not only small at 13” but also very slow to respond and the entire hard product was no better than it’s own Premium Economy product on it’s newer A350s. It was the first time that I have not been able to get even a minute of shut-eye in a Business cabin. The cabin crew did well to make up for the abysmal hard product by providing exemplary service and meticulous attention to detail extending beyond just during the meal service. Their warmth partially made up for the disappointment and as a consolation, the flight arrived on time and check-in baggage did not go missing. One thing to note would be that most of the 777s in the Cathay fleet should already have undergone the retrofitting process to the updated 1-2-1 configuration using the Cirrus seat, which reclines into a fully flat bed and offers direct aisle access. The A350s come with the same configuration direct from the factory, bypassing the retrofitting process. These particular B777-non-ER 2-3-2 business class configuration which I am reviewing seem to be present predominantly on the shorter routes, used to regional destinations like Taipei, Seoul, Osaka and Tokyo.

The seats are cozy and it can recline to a full flat bed, bedding and pillow are soft. The business class has a 1x2x1 configuration and my seat was assigned on the right hand of middle section. It has ample personal space and storage. It has decent privacy as there is a divider in the middle which separates me from the passenger on the left hand side. It would be nice if they can add sliding door in each business class seat like other airlines.

Seats are definitely on the cramped and tight side on a 3x3x3 configuration in the economy class. If you want a comfortable seating position to rest and even take a nap, recommend picking the window seats, it has slightly more space. On the good side, aisles are slightly wider than the 3x4x3 configuration in some other aircraft types, so passengers should be able to walk down the aisle comfortably. The in-flight entertainment screen is awesome and every seat houses a USB charging port, which is somewhat rare in economy class despite more airlines begin to offer that.

Not the most comfortable seats in the class. The legroom is on the tight side, the seats are padded and soft. Cabin crew also gave us pillow and blanket to max out comfort for a short nap. Overall, there was nothing I can complain about. If you want extra comfort, go for some of the Middle East airlines.

Overall Cathay Pacific economy class seat is not top in the class but overall it's fine. Their seats have similar comfort than the competitors. Legroom is alright but I won't say it's top notch. Cathay Pacific offers pillow and blanket for each seat. I managed to have a decent 2 hour sleep. Cathay Pacific could certainly do better on the comfort of economy class seats.

The seats are alright, about the same as other airlines, head rest and shoulder rest comfort are acceptable but nothing surprising. The entertainment was great with one USB charging port available. There is 2 aisles in economy class cabin on the A330.

Sitting in those seats was the worst 16 hours of my life! I'm a tiny 5'3 frame and my shoulders were touching the two people next to me. One of them had their leg touching mine the entire time. I could not move my feet either because I had a bag stowed under the seat in front of me and there was no legroom left. The screen felt like it was right up in my face and there was hardly any reclining in the seats. The best part about the flight was going into the bathroom where I did not have to touch the person next to me or hear them breathe. I've been on many flights before including international ones with Cathay Pacific and never complained about the seats in economy. I heard they had condensed the seats a few years ago which is why the space was so small. I could tolerate a few hours flying like this, but 16 hours was well past my limit. Thankfully, I upgraded to Premium Economy flying back. The difference was day and night. I wasn't touching anyone and had plenty of legroom. Even as a budget traveler, it was worth every penny. Never again, Cathay Pacific.
No smooth boarding, very old cabin. Entertainment system outdated, very bad headphones provided. The food I wanted to select was already empty. Many scratches and dirt in seat environment.

Below standard business class seats despite new aircraft. Basically an Economy seat (42 cm Wide) fitted in a business class plastic shell with fixed armrests which cannot retract of be lowered. Arms devoid of support in bed position and so narrow that it makes you feel claustrophobic and squeezed in a narrow foot pit and plastic shell. No seat storage. Definitely not to standards and would not recommend. Boarding was hectic and delayed by more than 75 minutes without any announcement. The ground staff looked unprofessional.
Very spacious and comfortable seats. I'm very tall and I felt that I had enough space during the whole journey. The screen was also standards and movies were good.
Nice and comfy business class seat. The cabin staff were very attentive. I was offered business seat upgrade during my check in, which was a pleasant surprise, since my flight duration was 13hrs.

Really poor seats for a 6 hour flight, along with the price I paid, offered only an uncrowded ambiance tho little comfort. There is no way to get rest as the seat recline is limited. Never again! I suggest that you Do not fly the Panama / Brazilia route as these are small planes. Come to think of it as Brazilia is the capital of Brazil it would be a nice change to have a lie flat seat - or almost - for the almost 6 hour flight to Panama. I feel the airline should I advise the passenger of the limited offering on these flights. Time for a change?

Copa Airlines is very helpful, especially with seat assignments. I bought a last minute trip due to the fact that I had a very painful lumbago and I need to go back to the doctor ASAP. I called the customer service rep to request a wheelchair service for next morning since I could not walk and she added it without hesitation. The next morning I went to the airport to take the flight and, since I bought a last minute ticket my chair was 33C, the last row, really difficult to access for someone who cannot walk, and the rep issued me a better seat, 5D, really comfortable. In Panama, as well, they noticed my impairment and issued me 5F, really comfortable for my back. My special thanks to all the reps In Orlando and Panama who made this painful trip more tolerable; special thanks to Kimberly Martinez en Panama who got me a last minute comfortable chair. Because of this and punctuality of the schedules I highly recommend Copa Airlines.

Nice looking seat with adequate storage and large video screen. Unfortunately seat felt hard / uncomfortable after a few hours. Inflight bedding was soft and plush, but when the seat transformed into bed it still was not enough to help soften bed. Simply could not get comfortable. I really wanted to like this seat as its aesthetics were really nice. Definitely an improvement over the older Delta One, but the seats could benefit from a bit more cushioning.

Delta One was my first choice before covid but this time the seat layout, size, angle gave me the worst experience. The leg space for window suit was way too small. At full flat position, I couldn’t turn my body because my feet are stuck in the leg space. I had to make seat upright first to turn my body. The full flat seat is tilted too much, so my body was tense whole flight. I had a backache when I arrived in Seoul, then after taking the inbound flight( this time at center suite) I had a little more legroom but seat was still too steep, i started having a muscle tenderness (couldn’t walk or wake up) for 1 full day after the flight. Food was worse than before but still acceptable for Coming back flight. The food prepared in Seattle was so bad. As an appetizer, I had a half cut egg roll, fried shrimp, both were tasteless. Food prepared in Korea was a tasty chicken salad. Never fly Delta One any longer.

Very little legroom on the A319 (6’ 2”) but good legroom on a A320. Dark and old feeling cabin.  Small window which was low down and dirty. Noisy cabin from engines No recline on seat. Small tray table which hadn’t been cleaned.

Surprisingly good seat next to the window, 64A. 2 windows at this seat. USB charger as well as option for charging with a plug. Felt the personal entertainment screen was a good size. Watched 6 movies on the 16 hour flight. Since the flight was not full, economy passengers were spaced around the cabin mostly with a seat between them.

Narrow seats make an uncomfortable long haul flight. Service was okay, food is also good. But the biggest drawback is simply the cabin. Regardless the snazzy façade with wooden divider accent, mellow mood lighting theme, the 17.05" wide economy seat on 777-300ER is too awful when the seats are fully occupied. Bumping shoulder is expected, having to dislodge someone next to you from their seats when you try to find your seat belt or reach to your pocket is inevitable. They don't even try to make amends by increasing the pitch. It is just a meagre 32". As a small 5'9" (175 cm) person, it feels cramped already when the passenger in front of you reclined their seat. Cannot imagine using this aircraft to flew to LAX from TPE. Not worth anything beyond $50 per hour of flight, as the seat comfort is not any better than low cost carrier in their 737NGs (just slightly above 17").

Seat 3J Diamond seats, my IFE not working, changing screens without any inputs. Restarted and same issues after restart. Brought to attention of flight attendant who witnessed issue 30min before Geneva. System restarted again in Geneva, same issues of non-functioning IFE throughout flight. What is the point of paying for business class if they do not provide something as simple as IFE? Even the review screen had errors on it.

There are two configs on the A350, the 2x2x2 & the staggered seating. My preference is for the older seating it is less cramped. The seat/bed is comfortable. The meals are excellent especially the Ethiopian Cuisine. All the flights were on time and the service level on the aircraft exemplary. The Biz lounge at Addis is great, albeit a bit of a scrum 0700-1000 when all the transits/ transfers take place. I have used them twice on the UK -JNB route, better timings than EK or Qatar

Was much better than I thought the seat would be, okay legroom and recline, screen was satisfactory and there were adequate ports (USB, Power, AUX). Their A350s are much better than their 787s so find a route with the A350.
The most uncomfortable seats. I am a small person and I still felt claustrophobic, which is unusual for me on flights. The seats were very uncomfortable, after 30 minutes it hurt to sit.

May 2025 brought with it a refresh to the American Airlines B787 fleet, as part of this refresh it included new seat cushions to the economy cabin seats. These were to provide ‘extra comfort’, unfortunately the rigidness of the foam provides very little noticeable ‘comfort’ apart from the thickness difference which brings new problems for taller or larger passengers. As someone over 6ft, my comfort comes into question if my shoulders go above the headrest, or the armrests are too low for my elbows to rest comfortably on them. The extra thickness of these new cushions caused exactly that, I was unable to fold the headrest wings because I was sat too high for the highest headrest setting, my thighs were above the armrests and so my elbows only reached them if I slouched awkwardly. The final issue I had is I had to pull the seatbelt out to its full length, usually I have about 6-8inches of slack on the seatbelt. I dread to think what a larger passenger would do, risking the need for a seat belt extender! American needs to revert to the old 2 inch thick seat cushions, these ones were a bad decision.

I consider American Airlines a world-class carrier with aspirations for excellence, so when I sat down at my seat and found the touch screen was not working. I thought, “Ok, it’s fine; this sometimes happens. This is okay.” Then I put my arm on the armrest and was surprised to see that the entire armrest was covered in duct tape, and I thought to myself, “Duct tape? really?!” If I rent a car, and upon getting in, find the seat is covered with duct tape, I would consider this unacceptable. So, for American Airlines, which has aspirations for excellence. My question is this: Is this acceptable?

Flight on a 737, business/first class is 16 seats in 4 rows. Seats are generally comfortable, wide, with adequate legroom. Other than that there is nothing to differentiate them from a coach seat. No longer get a screen, no longer get any kind of priority wifi service, no longer offered headsets, no big screen, no options. Connectivity is mediocre mostly. This is a 4 hour flight. All the airlines are the same with some route exceptions.

I was initially worried about that older AA product and concerned that seating backward might be uncomfortable. It turns out that I prefer seating backward in lie flat position because of the angle of attack of the plane. Your head remains above your feat and it feels better. I also enjoy the fact that the seat does not have a footwell which usually feels cramped. On the other AA B777 seat configuration I keep banging my knees at the top of the footwell when I move. There is consequently a little less storage available but I prefer the openness of the pod configured that way.

The seats are very narrow and big guy next to me extended several inches beyond. Most uncomfortable ride ever. the seats were redesigned recently to cram passengers. Love AA but now looking for more comfortable airline for international travel. 17" seats doesn't cut it!

Flying PHX-LHR, so long flight. Seat 39H I am 6'1", 210 lbs, so not outsize. Appalling seat design. Very narrow (10 abreast in a B777 should be a crime against humanity). Seat cushion surprisingly high, and, worse, rises when seat is reclined, jamming the knees against the back of the seat in front, and ensuring legs cannot be stretched under seat in front, making sleeping OR working virtually impossible - I am writing this sitting sideways, with legs and laptop in the aisle. Seat power supply does not appear to work. I normally fly BA on this route. The difference in seat quality is off the scale. Never again on AA.

Good food, modern aircraft, poor service. To AA's credit, the food was good and plentiful. But the crew didn't care if I enjoyed the flight and didn't seem to enjoy their work. They actually seemed more like old, tired police officers whose main intent is to force compliance with the rules. Jaded, overworked, unsmiling, unhappy people who have made this trip thousands of times but for whom passengers seem like an impediment to ending the crew's workday. PA system was so weak that I could not hear the announcements. Also, the crew can control the window tint, which they kept blackened for almost the entire flight. That makes the window seats into dark, black holes which I will never intentionally use again. Infotainment system is awkward and unimaginative. 110v power outlet is very difficult to reach, hidden behind an armrest. Need to have more USB-C outlets. Work on the ground in Tokyo was handled by Japan Airlines staff, who worked hard and were presentable. Unless I'm using AA frequent flyer miles I will use JAL (or, for that matter, any other airline) for my next trip to Japan.

I miss the old AA economy seats with IFE. The new seats introduced a few years ago stripped out the IFE and some seat padding. The new seats do offer more storage though. The WI-FI on board still is okay but not the best. The seats are survivable for 4 hours and the device holder is handy. Legroom remains the same and the seat width is better than the 737. The A320 family fleet of American Airlines is usually more comfortable than their Boeing aircraft. I do prefer the older seats with IFE though.

I paid extra in order to select a seat for my wife and myself toward the front of the plane. ( I guess). Flight was from Philadelphia to Ft Lauderdale. There was certainly no extra room involved. I selected a window and middle seat. Row 14. Boarding was a nightmare. They board in groups 1-8. You have to pay $34.00 in order to board in an early group. Just selecting an "extra room" seat for 2 people adds over $100.00 minimum to your cost. Otherwise you board, NOT from back to front, but apparently when you bought your ticket. You are allowed a carry on. except if you are in boarding groups 7 or 8. At the gate you will be told that if you are in groups 7 or 8, you must check your carry on.(Happens on full or nearly full flights). Since you selected a window seat you expect a window. Not on American. They jam so many rows on to the plane that about 30% of the window seats don't actually align with a window, so you are jammed against a blank bulkhead. No seat back entertainment. I am 6'1", so I don't consider myself overly tall. My knees were jammed against the seat in front of me, to the point where I could not really even access the seat pocket in front of me. The tray table was up against my chest. Not a great way to fly for 3 hours. For the way you get treated by this airline, you might as well fly Spirit or some other budget carrier and save on the fare. There is NOT comparison between this airline and competitors Delta, Jetblue, and United. Never again.

Seat 19C. Limited legroom for the economy seats. Wifi was ok but kicked me off more than once. The amount of recline seems to be about 10-15 degrees. Person in from of me reclined and almost caught my iPad. Width was normal for an economy seat. The seat was clean.

The seats are confusing. They do not match the outside row. 22 window seats match to 21 center row. Several people sat in the wrong seat — me too. Also center row seats E & G straddle a bar supporting the seat in front. So my underseat bag was placed weirdly, partly on my neighbors feet. The seats are narrower than the seats in my first leg of this trip. Otherwise its airy and as is customary - a half pinky finger biscuit with a beverage. Service is excellent!

Literally the smallest width seats possible. Sitting in the seat and the arm rest can't even go fully down. I'm 6'2", 220lbs. The oppression next to me weighs more and has an even wider hip span. We are sitting on top of each other to fit in the seats.

Miserable staff, poor customer service, and constant delays without communication to customers. No one seems to know anything. The plane was clean, but old. The wifi did not work. Avoid AA at all costs.

On my flight from PHL to BOS, I got a seat that was old. It was uncomfortable, with hard armrest, small tables, no IFE or power, fixed headrest, and minimal recline. It was just not a very good seat! At least the legroom was decent!

I am unhappy that despite speaking to a rep twice to ensure my family would be seated together, at check in we were separated. The worker at the gate could not have cared less. The airline does kit know anyone’s medical or immune status. Given Covid they should make lite if an effort to respect requests and if not, there is no need to be rude.

I flew many times with American Airline and majority of the time I flew Business or First Class. So I sort of knew what kind of service I will get. I also had flown other major airlines and American Airline Business Class in general is about average performance I don't recall any unfavorable experiences. What I experienced with AA Flight 700 from SFO-PHL on March 7th 2020 was absolutely deserve recognition due to Flight attendant Suzy. She showed warmth, customer service with focus on solution. After I settled down I first switched seat with fellow passenger in order to be seated in the center Isle with my husband. A while later Suzy came to take the food choice and she apologize for only oatmeal left. Suzy saw my hesitation, quickly said she will try to see what she can do, she eventually found a ham and egg tray with a lot of fruits. After I finish the meal I decide to lay flat for a while and realized the seat will not move or recline. She came to apologize and offer me some miles compensation without me asking for it. My experience with Suzy had a direct comparison with my husband's flight attendant. It was night and day. My husband also got an oatmeal breakfast, but it was coldly announced to him without apology and no other interaction during the 5 hours flight. In contrast Suzy walk along the isle to fill my hot water, very attentive. Suzy needs to be recognized.

I chose one of the best seats on this older configuration of 787. It was a window forward facing seat. They offer mattress, duvet and pillow. The seat length was very long but slightly narrow. The only storage was big enough for most stuff.

I was shocked to see how close the rows were placed. I am an average height woman and have never had a flight where my knees almost touched the back of the seat in front. Getting in and out was very difficult, particularly if the person in front was reclining. In fact, when they reclined, it was best to also recline. I had a 12+ hour flight, followed by a 6+ hour flight, too long to be so cramped. The seats were more narrow that usual and the aisles also narrow, I wasn’t sure until my return journey with another airline.Their seats are definitely wider, as are the aisles and there was much more room between the row seats. It was so obvious that when my son & I boarded, I remember saying to him 'this feels like business class after the trip over.' He was shocked as he flew the other airline both ways. Sadly for this reason, I would never fly with Etihad again.

The worst service and horrific baggage handling practices! This was a round trip. It started well on the way to our holiday with a relatively good service. It all changed on the flight home to Melbourne. Shortly after locating my seat, I discovered that it was wet smelling like urine. It took my fellow passenger going directly to one of the staff for them to actually address my wet seat and replace it. This is the airline I will definitely avoid at all cost!

We were fortunate enough to get the extra legroom seats but were not able to sit together because the staff on Etihad phone service refused to link our bookings, which were booked separately. Their entire raison detre is to get you off the phone with no action on their part. The cabin crew and ground staff were great. Food was so so. The main beef is a full service airline should not be charging for standard seat selection. On that basis we will never fly Etihad again.

Had the pleasure of experiencing the Business Studio product on the 787-10, and while it is  7 years old, it still is among my favorites. It offers a 180 degrees full flat bed and a handy control on the side of the seat and on the Inflight Entertainment screen. The seat comes with a bunch of adjustable features, such as seat cushion and a massage feature. I found the seat to offer a great amount of privacy. Also managed to get some work done while flying, the table is big enough and doesn't move too much. Very satisfied with this seat, would book again!

Very unhappy. Booked a forward facing window seat well over a moth prior to the flight, and even when checking in online the night before that seat was showing as my reserved seat. After arriving at the airport my seat was changed. When asked they could only tell me there was no comment as to why my seat was changed. Now I’m riding backwards on the aisle and over the engine instead of being tucked away by the window and having a forward facing seat ahead of the noise of the engine. Incredibly disappointed and my next business trip will be through Dubai with a drive to Abu Dhabi. 4 stars because the crew was good and the food was good. But not getting what was paid for is pretty terrible. I personally hate the Etihad business configuration. The new United polaris is similar but is much better with no rear facing seats.

The seat was very comfortable with enough legroom for someone as tall as me (6'3). I liked the width which was ok for a long-haul flight, the seat offers recline and has an Inflight Entertainment System, which features a ton of movies, tv-series, games, music, and much more. The seat even has a USB port so you can charge through the power outlet.

While the A380 Business Class is fine the A330-200 Business is worse than flying Regional Jet in my opinion. The screen is broken and small and I cannot access their entertainment either.  The power plug does not work either. Apart from the seats that is so awful design I see. The service is even worse as budget airlines either. Never fly Etihad again.

Worst seating I've experienced outside of discount airlines. Seat in front of me was mere inches from me and it is uncomfortable and claustrophobic on a 12-hour flight.
