My second flight was worse, as the seats did not recline. They have crammed the seats in the plane so close together that the seats, literally, can not be reclined, so they've disabled the buttons. I had high expectations based on Etihad's reputation, which made the reality and second class citizen feel of the flight all the more surprising. The food was OK at best. Service was nothing to remember. My experience makes me think that Etihad is an airline that you would only want to fly business or first class with. On the plus side, Etihad offers a two day stay in Abu Dhabi that is a great experience, and I was happy with that part of the package, but I will avoid flying Etihad in the future.

Seat 4A on Flair’s Boeing 737-800 is good. You get 2 windows and a nice view of the engine, but 5A is better for that view. When I flew the 4A, B, and C row was empty except for me. Seat felt kind of hard though. On my flight it had a charging outlet, but didn’t work

These seats are the worst. First off they're stained and filthy, they are barely wide enough for an average adult, my waste is 34 and I was very uncomfortable. I had paid for bulkhead row as I knew the legroom was tight, and even there I wasn't comfortable at all. $60 for extra legroom and I couldn't even cross my legs because I'd be within the wall, the seats are too close to the walls of the cabin, and they don't recline so you're very uncomfortable the entire flight.

More than I expected. Flights were on time, service was good, you get what you paid for, fares are very reasonable, and love having a direct flight from point A to point B. Only caution though is on the legroom - row 5 A/B/C very light compared to the other side of the row 5 D/E/F.

Better that expected. After reading some of these reviews we were a little concerned. My wife and mother-in-law travelled Saskatoon to Vancouver. We decided to give Flair a try due to the very high rates from Air Canada and Westjet. The booking was very easy. If you travel with just a carry-on it is very cheap. Checking bags is where they recover their discounted rates. ~$75/bag. Expensive but still significantly cheaper than AC and WJ. The booking was easy. Regular reminders can on our phones and email. Check-in on-line was very easy. The plane left on time and arrived on time. The staff at the gate were very helpful and courteous. My wife noted how helpful Betty was. She was an air hostess on the plane. The plane was smooth on take off and landing. Overall a good experience. We will fly Flair again. At least we have another choice. When people write a review they should write it based on a "Discount" airline.

Night flight from PVR to YVR. 5 hour duration, departing 2100. All seats are permanently locked upright with no choice to recline at all. It simply punishes its passengers in doing this with no real common sense at all, especially on a night flight.

Never again. The seats are incredibly close together. In case of an emergency, I doubt many people could get out in an efficient manner. There are seats with more leg room but you have to pay a premium for that. The seats are hard and uncomfortable. They also do not recline. This makes sense because you would recline into the person's face behind you. On top of that, the Flair App kept crashing so no in-flight entertainment. I know this is a discount airline but the experience was worse than bottom basement pricing. The flight had only 29 passengers with capacity for 186. When I asked to move to a seat with more leg room I was denied since I did not pay for that. 30 minutes into the flight I moved anyway and got dirty looks from the flight attendant. She did not approach me though, maybe because she realised how ridiculous it was to deny me.

It was my first time flying Flair airlines and I was really curious about what the ULCC would deliver. I had read all about their poor on time departure performance and customer service issues and was prepared for anything they threw at me. I have no complaints whatsoever. We did purchase the big bundle and had priority boarding so this we super smooth as well. I sat in their preferred section where there was extra legroom and felt is was also great - Seat 3F. My only complaint here is that this specific seat is narrower than others perhaps due to the shape of the fuselage. I would not recommend row 3 again. At least Row 4 if the Window seat is desired. And as expected we departed more than an hour later than scheduled. but overall a good experience. I would recommend them for leisure travellers who are not making any connection and really want the bare bones experience (no power, no entertainment).

The arrogance and disrespect for my daughter. On both flights she was bullied out of her window seat by a family looking to seat their children at the window. On the first flight a family took advantage of early boarding for families. Kate arrived to the window seat I booked her and found a dad on the aisle and his five year old kid in her window seat (maskless, btw). He said his kid wanted to sit next to the window. Then another man came up and told the father in the window seat that he was sitting in his seat. So the father moved across the aisle, leaving her in the middle seat between a stranger and a random 5 year old without a parent.  I paid for that seat for her. This family had the opportunity to do so as well. Kate didn't want to have to complain to the father or out loud to the flight attendant and make trouble. Kate was texting me all this from the plane. I found out later that during the ascent the father had to attend to his five year old so got out of his seat to do so. The flight attendants got mad. Said he couldn't leave his kid and insisted on getting everyone to their correct seat. Then this morning as she was boarding her flight, same thing happened. Different family. At least they asked her this time. They wanted to be seated together. Now she's on the aisle. I told her to tell the flight attendant but she has decided not to as she'd be stuck on the inside with their screaming baby. Why bother offering to pay for seats if none of it matters anyway? The flight attendants should have to demand everyone sits in seats that are unpaid for. Not have to rely on paying customers to sort it out. It's terrible how she was put in this situation. A tiny 16 year old on her first flights alone.

Their business class in the A380 is average in the 777 is terrible at best. Seats are bad! Food is so bad! Lounges are bad. Their business model to make money definitely works, their experience is horrendous

Seats on the aircraft were old and outdated, and had seen better days. Inflight entertainment system reflected this with slow responsiveness. Seats offered little lumbar support, leaving the traveler after a long haul flight needing a soft surface to recover. The seats were extra legroom, bulkhead seats with no under seat storage.
Seat 57g aisle seat must have been one of the most threadbare and uncomfortable seats i have ever had the misfortune to be seated on. Food was way below par from what it once was.

I had booked 6 Business class tickets and was seated in the 11th row, however, one of them was defective and wouldn't recline. The crew tried to fix it to no avail. They highlighted that the plane is full and confirmed that 2 other seats of "staff confirmed booking" refused to swap with a full paying customer. I paid nearly AED14,000 per ticket! To compound things further, the service was horrendous, the head stewardess had an extremely bad attitude and they didn't even serve me my order until i went to inquire about it because they forgot. The Purser threatened me to delete the footage of the malfunctioned chair otherwise she would notify security to meet me upon landing. This is what it has come down to with what used to be one of the best airlines in the world. Daylight robbery, bullying, and a snobby attitude!

This is a specific review of 68K I flew 68K on both legs LGW-DXB and DXB-SIN. This is an outstanding seat for legroom. If legroom is your priority, even with your own access to the seat, this is THE seat to go for in economy along with its corresponding seat on the port side. The legroom is basically full stretch and you can access in and out viw the gap in front with so much room that you won’t annoy the two seats to your diagonal front. There’s no danger of the people in your row using your corridor, especially if you extend the video monitor. The downside of this seat is of course no at seat storage for take off and landing, and the video monitor is a bit rubbish as is the flimsy tray extension. Neither USB port worked on my flights either. But it’s all about legroom and this excels.

If you are considering booking extra leg room seats on an Emirates flight don’t. While their normal seats are comfy with sufficient leg room regrettably the same cannot be said about their extra leg room seats. These are situated next to the toilets, the tv screen is in a section of the seat making them narrower than the regular seats and less comfy. The main problem is that the lights from the toilets do not dim and make it difficult to sleep. In addition the space in front of you “your extra leg room” is continually used by people queueing for the toilet. We would therefore advise that you stick to the normal seats and save yourself some money.

I'm not a tall person, but I struggled to be comfortable I had 2 flights each way via Dubai. 7 hours to Dubai, then 9 hours plus to Narita, then 12.5 hours back to Dubai then 8 hours back to Glasgow. Unfortunately on the way out I could hardly move and I ended up getting Cellulitis which left me unwell and put dampener on the holiday. All seats I could hardly move , my lower back was constantly in pain which left me struggling to get off my seat even to go for a walk around the cabin, make things worse the seat was broke from NRT-DXB crew couldnt help and ICE System didn't work either, leaving me with a very bad Emirates experience.

Got in the seat, everything was fine first 30 mins then felt like I was sitting on solid concrete or even wood, lower back so painful I couldn't move until I landed in Dubai second flight wasn't as bad as there was no one sitting next to me had a little more room, still couldnt move. The main problem was the meals, Nearly less than a year before I travelled (I can't remember exactly Dec 22-Feb 23) I contacted There call centre that I have food allergies (wholemeal items, mushroom, fish) and I already knew especially second flight those items were on the menu. The online help agent said bring your own meals, I made him aware they will be taken off me at departing airport, he said they wouldnt, they were taken off me. Then advised take the bland meal option you'll be fine, first option had mushroom, second meal had fish. I felt unwell for a hour or so onboard, The crew was surprised when I hand the whole meal back untouched when they collected rubbish. I go every year to Japan, the time on emirates are great as the return gives me virtually the full last day, others I lose it, for 2024 or 2025 I will be using another airline. The "help" desk is terrible. I've been in so called airlines considered not as good customer service who have been great. I know my return back to Dubai I have the same problem awaiting help desk said there is nothing they can do, not there problem.

Got to my seat, width was lovely, Leg room was great, reclining seat marvellous. After 15 minutes it was the worst comfort i have ever had in a seat ever, long haul or short haul. Felt like I was sitting on a plank of wood for every journey i made.  Everything else was great, please put another review for overall comfort as these seats are terrible.
The 777 are awful to fly in. Ridiculous, narrow seats and limited legroom. In comparison to the A380, with wide seats and better legroom. Seats a bit hard after 15 hours.

During this flight, there was a child seated directly in front of me who attempted to throw things at myself and my seat mates, kept touching my screen, would not stay seated and parents would not control him. When I alerted the stewardess  she said "give it a minute". His behavior continued on and off about ever 20-30 minutes during this 14+ hour flight. I asked to be moved to another seat. At first, I was informed that the flight was fully booked. The 3rd time I asked to be moved, she moved me to one open seat which happened to be by the bathroom. So I was moved from one noisy, loud, and overly active and disruptive child to a seat where I could now smell the toilets, which created nausea. When I was returning to the original seat by the overly active and disruptive child, she said "Are you having one of those days? I'm sorry but there's nothing I can do for you?" It wasn't that there was nothing she could do, it was that she chose to do the very least and that was nothing. There was open seating in business class and she did not offer which is ridiculous customer service. This child was throwing things, the parents refused to control the child. They let the child sleep on the floor several times when another stewardess informed them that the child could not sleep on the floor. She could not control the parents of the child nor the child and refused to assist me to have a peaceful experience on the 14+ hour flight I paid for. It's as if my investment in the ticket was not as good as theirs. When I pressed the button for a stewardess she was no where to be found as the flight went on. I had an amazing flight going to Dubai, the staff of flight EK0236 was very friendly but this one stewardess for flight EK0235 ruined my entire experience by not rectifying the situation with the child and the parents. Who wants to sit in a plane for 14hr having thing thrown at them or the child touching their screen while they are trying to watch a movie? It was unbearable and unbelievable.

My initial booking was on Economy class and then I upgraded to business class after paying fare difference. Business class seat was uncomfortable. If you're seating on window seat and wanted to move from your seat you will not be able to leave your seat unless you disturb passenger that sitting next to your seat. And if passenger next to you is laying down and sleeping then you need to jump to pass or you must wake up him/she to move seat to seating position. Furthermore, service on board was not to level to business class as I was expecting. In addition, was surprised upgraded ticket was not included using airline lounge in Dubai Airport. Finally it is not worth paying so much money for upgrade to Business class on B787 300 aircraft.

This was a Boeing 777-300ER on one of Emirates' older aircraft that did not have  lie-flat seats.  The drawback I would find on this flight was the 2x3x2 configuration (no direct aisle access for window seats and the one middle seat) and how uncomfortable the seat is especially while sleeping.

This was one of Emirates newer business class seats which go lie flat making it comfortable to sleep in.  The seat was wide enough to sit comfortably and was long enough for me to sleep in (I'm 6'2"). Complimentary wifi for skywards members in business worked well and was enough to text. IFE screen was clear and the amenity kit was well stocked. The only drawback I can find with this seat is the lack of privacy on the aisle seats and how hard it is to get onto the aisle when on a window or middle seat.

We were a family of five, and our seats were one middle row plus one seat on the middle-left aisle in front of the middle row we occupied. Seat was comfortable and came with blanket, pillow and pair of headphones and toys for children. The IFE system is the best of airlines we’ve travelled. Most of the content on the system is in English, but there are options in other languages. TV is large. Selection of entertainment for kids was excellent. All seats with a USB port and most seats also with a three-prong electrical socket. Storage space for baggage is ample. Legroom is sufficient for tall passengers.

Emirates Boeing 777 is a sub standard plane nowadays. Business class layout 2x3x2 is obsolete and very uncomfortable. This is the only business class on long haul that you almost don’t have space for your shoulder and I am pretty small. If you are tall forget to seat here comfortable . It’s unbelievable how poor is the design of this aircraft. Never pay for business class on 777, never ever is an uncomfortable premium economy. I am a frequent flyer with Emirates but the business class in Emirates is sub standard, big gap with any premium airline . Terrible that Emirates such old plane and seat.

Horrible seats, not comfortable at all. Dirty seats in business class. Definitely not worth the big price tag for thousands of euros. Avoid if you are looking for comfort or cleanliness over a flight. And the food is horrible.
Good seats, a little better than average, very good tv. The tv has a lot of options, exterior camera view, very good map. Nice quality and good chargers.

Bearable seats with storage space underneath the seats; however, the TV entertainment is awful. The screen is sluggish and not too touch sensitive. I've a hard time navigating the menu and movies/shows. Improvements needed.

I'm not expecting extreme seating comfort on a budget airline, but the quality of the seats in Flydubai is rather poor. Seats are lightly padded and flimsy, legroom is tight considering I'm just 5 feet 5 only. The seats can recline but minimal, which offers little to no extra comfort in addition to the uncomfortable seats already. I was surprised the is a touchscreen infotainment screen. The infotainment screen does offer an array of movies and trip information. I do not recommend flying with Flydubai. The seat comfort is mediocre and uncomfortable.

Flight attendants and active flight staff are fantastic, however customer service and seat design is atrocious. I ended up collapsing on the flight and had to be walked off by emts, tried to change my return ticket to another member of my family as its clearly unsafe for me to fly and the fee was insane. Basically would have been buying a new ticket. Now to the seats on the flight, if you in anyway have a medical condition that is triggered by positional sensitivity then frontier is NOT for you. You cannot lean forward to put your head on the tray and you can in no way shape or form lean back. In order to restore my blood pressure I have to be reclined or supine-neither of which are remotely possible on a frontier flight. Ended up laying on the floor (which left black marks on all my clothes as the floors were very dirty) in front of the bathroom because there is no safe place on this plane in case of medical emergency. Also the space between passengers is non existent-as a 120lb 5’10” extremely slender woman I was absolutely eclipsed by the two passengers on either side of me. Flight attendants 10/10, passenger comfort and humanity of customer service- 0/10.

Genuinely awful! Like flying cross-country in a lawn chair. I’m only slightly above average height and I had to wedge my legs into place with my arms. Seats don’t recline, don’t have power sources, and don’t have TVs.

This was my second trip on Frontier from Philadelphia to Cancun and back. The trips were 17 days apart. On both trips I upgraded to “stretch seat”, it is worth it, there is one particular seat above the wing (photo attached) that does not have a seat in front that is the best seat if you don’t mind being on the wing right next to an engine. From Philadelphia to Cancun was about four hours and three hours coming back. These seats held up well for that time and I was as comfortable as I could be for the product offered. An additional benefit of the stretch seats is that you can also recline. The tray tables are super small but you really don’t need them for much, so their size did not matter to me. Frontier is an ultra low cost airline so you pretty much get what you pay for, if you can spare the extra money, go for the stretch seating on flights that are three hours or longer.

We paid extra for specific seats but did not get them and did not get a refund. Seats have fabric covering over hard plastic. No padding as would be expected with an upholstered seat. Not very comfortable for a long flight. Tight spaces but similar to other airlines in that respect.

Great experience on Eva Air. I travel a lot for work and company policy only allows for PE on long haul. EVA Air was a cut above on this leisure trip from Singapore to Vancouver via Taipei. Seats were very comfortable, the service was super professional and friendly, with the cabin crew very attentive. Some of the key differences over other airlines PE offering, was the supply of a proper and good quality amenity kit by Furla; plus a dedicated bathroom for PE customers. Also the food was really high quality and more like a business class offer than economy. My only criticism would be the IFE entertainment choices in English, which were comparatively limited. All in we had a very comfortable trip, with great service at a very reasonable price. I would travel with them again without hesitation and definitely in preference to Singapore Airlines, where routes allow.

The seat is uncomfortable and the tray table is unusable if you neighbor in front reclines his seat.  Usage of infotainment system is also difficult, since reclined seat in front, will bring the screen very close to your face.

Outstanding seats, Boeing 777-300 seats are very comfortable and the amenity kit along with the plush bedding, mattress and comforter was perfect for the long haul flight. The new 787 Royal Laurel class seats are very spacious and comfortable as well.

The experience is better than many North American and European Airlines. The staff are still outstanding and professional. Nothing is too much trouble and the food is excellent. In flight services are all about the passenger and nothing is too much trouble. The seats are comfortable and for a 16 hour plus flight, this is essential. The only problem is that EVA Airlines keep the cabins very warm, to the point of hot. I woke literally soaked through with sweat which is exacerbated by the rules that masks must be worn unless eating. The warm temperature also seems counterintuitive when considering that this temp is ideal for illness but again, it is something that EVA can control. This is a small issue but it affects the comfort of the flight. Apart from that, the airline continues to maintain a strong focus on service.

This was my tenth time flying on EVA air royal laurel class between Taiwan and US. The seat was really comfortable and provided a decent space for me to rest. The meal was fantastic too. And the cabin crews were friendly and provided excellent service which made it a very comfortable journey.

I will no longer be flying with them due to the 3-4-3 seat configuration on the Boeing 777. I accept that EVA are not alone in this layout but for a long haul flight the seating is inappropriate. Having paid extra for exit row seating I feel this made little difference and would hate to imagine what the normal seat experience would be.

Seat was ok, can't say comfortable really. Unfortunately the inflight entertainment system wasn't working for me and my family ( 4 seats) we weren't given any alternative seats and when I got back to the gf customer support - they only had an apology concerning the in-flight entertainment and told me that they will forward to relevant department. I regret choosing gulf air. Even the customer support wasn't satisfactory - when I replied to them with my concerns in the emails - the support wrote to me in the 2nd email that he/ she doesn't want to elaborate further... we faced flight delay and no in-flight entertainment on our seats - really sad. Such service is not expected and not satisfied at all

My flight was from Mumbai to Bahrain and then Bahrain to Istanbul. The flight from Mumbai to Bahrain was good with good seats and reclining. Bahrain to Istanbul was a normal seat (one cannot sleep) but that depends on the aircraft chosen (I understand) but the reclining option was not working. So I was on a Business Class Seat, late in the Night and the seat was not reclining. It was super uncomfortable and the Staff said 'Sorry" as nothing could be done and other seats were full.

I have chosen to give this airline an 8/10 review because the product was exceptional and the soft product, whilst still very good, is a bit underwhelming.  I boarded the plane and was warmly welcomed by the crew as they pointed to my seat, 2D. They promptly served a variety of pre-departure beverages from which I choose the fresh orange juice. Quality Arabic coffee was also served at this time. hot and cold towels were also distributed and the crew came round to ask for our meal choices. Once the plane had finished refueling, we began to take off for Bahrain. Soon after reaching the cruising altitude, I began to watch a movie and starters were served. Unfortunately, the cabin crew gave me the wrong starter. Upon bringing it up to them, they gave a rather sincere apology and gave me the correct starter of a simple yet tasty mozzarella salad. After that, mains were served and I got a rich chicken à la king with apple juice to drink. There was a noticeable gap in service between mains and desserts but I eventually got my dessert of a chocolate cake with tea. Soon after, I went to sleep after reminding the crew to wake me up for breakfast. I might have slept too deeply because the crew couldn't wake me up but fortunately, they still had breakfast available but it was not something to write home about. There was a selection of dry pastries which were worse than my economy meal. Soon after that we landed in Bahrain Airport. Overall I would say that the seat was exceptional but the food could be better in some way. Also, the crew did an exceptional job and I can understand why they left me to sleep.

Seat quality is fairly average. The seats are not comfy but acceptable for short haul flight. No entertainment screen so I watched movies from my iPad. There's USB ports where you can charge your devices and gadgets.

I recently flew with Garuda Indonesia from Jakarta to Shanghai, and it was a very disappointing experience. The seat was extremely uncomfortable, making the long flight unbearable. To make matters worse, the seat was dirty and had an unpleasant smell. The seat was too straight, preventing my neck from relaxing.  I noticed other passengers complaining about the same issues, and everyone kept adjusting their body positions to try and feel better. I expected much better service and will think twice before flying with Garuda Indonesia again.

The seats in these configurations are wider and you have quite a lot of legroom. As we are just short persons (1.7m) we didn't need very much legroom and this was fine for us in this setup. I can imagine however, that people with long legs, might want to book special places where you have more space. The in-flight entertainment was allright, a lot of games where supplied, which you can control with a game-controller that is stored in the arm-rest of each seat. The reclining of the seats is acceptable, but you can't go very far. Of course, this is understandable because of the fact that the person behind you also likes to keep some space. Storing stuff underneath the seats isn't very high, and my bag full of office stuff didn't really fit. In the overhead storage it wasn't any problem though. Each seat offered 110-230VAC power as well as USB outlets for charging your phone etc. - please do mind that the USB output is only at low amperage due to power distribution in the plane (which makes sense of course).

Seat layout was quite good in that there appears more knee room than other airlines with similar aircraft. The seats themselves, I thought were terrible. Little shape and a headrest that is too far from your head. So I could not lean back to rest my head without straining my neck. Perhaps all that model of aircraft are like that? I will take more notice on future flights.

First and last flight with Hong Kong Airlines. Assured of good flying weather we had the seat belt sign on due to turbulence. Also a unpleasant, checkin on line, catch. Unless you pay for a seat at online check-in you cannot complete the check-in online and avail yourself of a bag drop. The airbus Hong Kong to Osaka was tired worn and not checked for seat maintenance. My seat 55J kept on reclining, I asked for an alternative and not offered one, no apology just continually told to return it to upright for take off.. The seat in front in lay back protruded as per photo. Clearly not only my seat was in a state of disrepair. Seat coverings were also showing signs of wear and lack of care and the seat cushion flattened not offering much support.

The fully lie-flat seats made for a good night’s rest, even if it was only for a couple of hours. I could stretch out fully at a height of 5’10” (180cm). Storage space and seat width and comfort is very much in line with the standard of international carriers but not exceeding expectations, hence their rating as a Skytrax 4-star Airline is just about right.

The legroom and width comfort is about the same as the other A320 aircrafts. They are still considerably comfy but restricted for short flights. The aisle is also wide enough to walk pass thanks to its comparably wider aircraft.

JAL Sky Suite III - reverse herringbone.  Tight space, claustrophobic and uncomfortable. It might work if you are a very small person but it's shocking for a long haul flight. Be aware that JAL has many different business class seat types on their B787 and this is the worst, though the latest. Skysuite II is vastly better and preferable, even though it is 2x2x2 but with staggered layout.

The best feature of the JAL Premium Economy product is the seat. Encased in a shell like in Business class, no one can recline into your space and when you recline to have a nap, your feet move comfortably under the seat in front of you - even when you have hand luggage there. This might be less comfy if you are super tall but regardless, the leg rest and footstool combo keep the legs elevated which means you can turn onto your side. Pillow & blanket were comfy and the headrest was moldable so I actually slept - and the first stretch was a 14 hour flight. The seat was not hard and the result was that I felt quite fresh after each flight as I could get some sleep.
The seat was good and comfortable enough for 1 hour+ flight. The width is big enough for my body. The legroom is modest. Adjustable headrest well function. Lucky enough to occupy all three seats.

I have never experienced such little legroom as on my latest Iberia flight MAD - MVD. Almost 13 hours flight but you get less legroom than on a low cost airline. The overhead storage is ridiculously small. Really disappointed in Iberia. Feel like it wasn’t this bad before.

The seats are narrowest I have ever travelled on. I am a rather tall person (193cm) and I avoid low cost airlines because their seats are too narrow. If I knew that Iberia is operating as a low cost company, I would have preferred another airline.

The seat is a lie-flat. But it is extremely narrow compared to competition and very worn out. Seat cushions also worn out, so no help for comfort. The possibility to store your personal items is very unpractical and nothing to store your glasses during the night. The dashboard to move the seat has no light so most unpractical at night. The electrical plug did work. The tray is pretty wide but only has 2 positions: up or down! impossible to get it closer to you when eating.

Iberia Premium Economy on the A330-300. The plane was 7 years old but the cabin did not show its age. The cabin was very clean and kept immaculate. Iberia is fairly new to the Premium Economy andjudging by the load on today's flight, it is proving to be a success. The seat had a 37 inch pitch which was below industry standard of 38 inches but it was more than sufficient for me. I am not a tall person (5'8) and was able to stretch my leg and have a comfortable nap even with the person in front of me reclining all the way. The recline was outstanding and was able to get 3 hours uninterrupted sleep. The seat was 18.1 inches wide which was almost the same as Cathay Pacific's pre-refit Boeing 777-300ER which again kept me comfortable and having broad shoulders. Overall, Iberia's Premium Economy product is a great way to fly across the Atlantic.
Airbus 320neo. Horrible seat pitch my knees touched the front seat.  No comfort I had to sit sideways. The seats are semi hard and narrow width.

As it's a scheduled airline, there's little you can really say is special about the seat. It looks good, and the red ambiance is surprisingly calming and friendly on the eyes (especially at night). We purchased extra legroom which was a necessary for someone tall, standard legroom looked acceptable but tight for anyone wanting a comfortable flight despite being short haul. The seat was also relatively padded and supportive so that once I reached the destination, I was comfortable.

Completely horrible seats. We booked and paid a fairly significant premium for allegedly extra seats in row 1DEF. A disgusting rip off by Jet2. These seats are appalling. If they provide extra legroom, it is a tiny amount and not worth the ridiculous rip off amount this increasingly third rate airline charges. Compared to Easyjet and they fail on every level except the crew. They are unfailingly pleasant and hard working.

Low cost seats. The seats are so uncomfortable, no padding. I’ve had more comfort on a bus. It’s just Ryanair in red. For the price paid for the flight you’d expect more. The prices are no longer cheap.

My issues are the seats are too hard for the 4+ hour flight to Gran Canaria (general feeling amongst all those whose backside was numb by the time the plane landed). They won't pay for a terminal link but coach everyone out to the plane, this means the flights are always late taking off.

I flew ITA Airways on flight AZ857 (14 Oct 2025) and was assigned seat 33F, an emergency-exit row seat. Only after take-off did I discover that the seat did not recline at all. This was not indicated during booking, check-in, or boarding. On a 6.5-hour overnight flight, being unable to recline made it impossible to rest and resulted in a very uncomfortable journey. Exit-row seats are usually sold as extra legroom, so ITA should disclose when a seat cannot recline so passengers can make an informed choice.
Resembles a low fare/low cost airline but with premium fares. Absolutely no difference. Any person taller than the average 1.75m will for sure have troubles to accommodate.

Zero comfort, unfit to anyone taller than 1.60m, old fashion 1980's bulky seats, does not recline, in immediate contact to the wall behind. Unbelievably ITA charges premium fares and delivers less than low cost airlines quality.

I recommend sitting in rows 6 and 7 on Icelandair's 737 aircraft. There is better legroom than in seats at the rear of the aircraft and the screens are on the seatback, rather than in the seats in row 5, which are in the armrest and quite small. I recommend avoiding selecting seats in row 5 of Icelandair's B737 aircraft.

Do you relish the thought of the seat in front of you being mere inches from your face when you take an international flight? How about dreaming of your backside numb for hours on end because there is no viable escape if you are in a window seat? What are your thoughts on a cabin temperature kept to a steady 80 degrees? If these things, and experiences just like them, are your idea of a good time, forge ahead. I’ve been to Iceland around 40 times since 2012. I tolerated the increasingly ancient 757s interiors because I knew the Max 8 was coming. It seems like a lost opportunity. The seating experience is just so bad that any attempt to overcome via in flight service and amenities is lost. One less row in this plane and you can be a human. I fly all manner of classes for work all over the world. Often I get the great lie flat business class seats because I am a United 1k member but I also often am in economy, and that’s OK. It evens out. But this is just ridiculous.

Since covid I've tended to choose business class to ensure my wife and I can avoid sitting close to strangers and travel in our own bubble. That's why I chose Icelandair Saga class. We were booked on a B757 with a 2x2 configuration and checked in with seats 4D and 4F (window and aisle). But at the last moment the aircraft was switched to a B767 with 2x1x2 configuration. 4D became a orphaned middle seat with 4F across the aisle and an unknown stranger in the new window seat 4G. I wouldn't have known except for monitoring the inbound aircraft on Flight Radar 24. We protested at the gate and the agent told us no F and Gs were available, despite this flight's having been booked as a B757. Eventually she gave in and moved us, though only by shunting some other miserable passenger out of 4G that she hoped would make less fuss. Icelandair promote "free seat selection" as a reason for choosing Saga class, yet their unreliability as to which aircraft they're using turns it into a lottery. Apart from this bad start, we found the seats comfortable, but ours was a relatively short flight (KEF-LHR). Transatlantic passengers need to be aware of what they're getting: a wide reclining seat similar to short-haul domestic first class in the USA, but certainly no sleeper. The IFE is varied but the screens are annoyingly unresponsive. Very nice headphones, though.

Seat was very hard and there was no recline. The legroom is fine if you're short, but if you are of average height (say 5'6" or more), you are going to struggle. No pouch to store anything, just a bare basic leather seat

Hawaiian Airlines refers to their Premium Economy seats as Extra Comfort. The seats on the A-330 is 18 inches and the pitch is 36 inches. Even with my backpack under the seat in front of me I am able to be fairly comfortable, even at 5'11. The general comfort is adequate, not luxury. Padding on the sets is fine for the six hours and 45 minutes you spend on the plane from boarding to deplaning when flying from the west coast. I have never had a problem with the IFE, though the selection could use a little more updating. Each IFE screen has USB charging ports and there is universal power for the Extra Comfort seats.

It was a full flight. Not much legroom. We sit in the 4 seats row for easy access to the toilets. I’d recommend to pay extra legroom near the exit door rows. Flight attendant were nice. Inflight meal and entertainment was good.
The middle seat is very squishy. I’d recommend choosing an aisle seat and as upfront as possible. It’s worth to pay for extra legroom in the exit door rows.

Rows squeezed in so tight that even as a 166cm short man who is not fat the tray table is touching my belly and I can’t even use it to write on without elbowing my neighbours. I don’t know how the tall man across the aisle from me is coping. We are also stuck on the tarmac waiting for the toilet holding tanks to be emptied. Been delayed half an hour already with no word on how long it will take to fix the problem (if we will depart at all). The seat pocket is too small for a drink bottle. I only flew Jetstar because it was cheap but I think I’ll stick to other airlines in future.

Luckily wasn't a long flight. I'm 6 foot 3 or 191 cm. My knees were rubbing on the seat, had no room for getting my legs to stretch underneath and if i was leaning with my back on the seat was even worse so I had to use an inflatable neck pillow to overcome it. Design not human or at least tall human friendly.

Despite originally paying extra for an exit row we were allocated an up-front seat, and that was bad for us. I am just on 6ft tall and my knees were rubbing the back of the seta in front. This was an overnight flight and they was no way I could get comfortable enough to get any sleep. The room is so tiny that the tray tables can't be lowered all the way to allow you to put any drinks or meals on them. Thank goodness the person in front of me didn't/couldn't recline their seat!

For a budget airline, the seat was pretty good! It was mostly clean and quite spacious. The aisle was quite cramped though and you really had to squeeze through. On newer planes you get a pocket to store things which is nice. There's a mostly clean tray table which moves easily. No power or screen though, so make sure you charge your devices!

Flying from JFK to Nairobi. Tried to upgrade my economy seat to business via Kenya Airways online bid system (offered several days before the flight), but my offer of $1700 per ticket was declined. I ended up pay a slight premium to move into bulkhead seats (25g & h), which was a great decision. These seats face the lavatory, which wasn’t an issue at all, and provided us with endless legroom. The seats are an exit row, so the armrests are fixed, but I did not feel the seat width was cramped. The seat recline is pretty decent, and the cushion extends out with the recline, so you can get yourself into a pretty acceptable position to sleep. The only downside is the seat cushions felt pretty thin/hard, so after a few hours you could start to feel a little bit of an ache. Overall, this was an acceptable option and probably worth the $3,400 I saved on my i upgrade bid since Kenya Business class is not really on par with other Asian/Mid-East carriers. Overall it was a good flight.

My business class seat 3D was broken and would not move. The staff took off the cushions and laid it flat with a manual handle where it stayed for the remainder of the 11hr flight AKL to SCL. When I contacted LATAM Customer Support they declined to offer any sort of recompense at all because an official report wasn't made by the staff, after she told me that she would.

LATAM's seating policy is one of the worst I’ve experienced. Unless you're willing to pay extra, you're stuck with the most uncomfortable middle seats. Seat selection isn’t included, and their system is designed to push you into paying more for basic comfort. The seats are cramped, with minimal legroom, and the recline is barely noticeable. For such long flights, this is unacceptable. On top of that, the staff showed no flexibility in helping passengers who requested better seating due to special circumstances. If you're looking for comfort, either prepare to pay a significant amount on top of your ticket or avoid LATAM altogether. Their seating arrangements are a money grab, and customer care doesn’t seem to care.
Economy layout with 2-4-2 but nice seat with great legroom (83 cm) and 45 cm seat wide. Seats are equipped with with big IFE sceen and power supply as well as the holder for own smartphone or tablet

One of the most comfortable Boeing 777-300 with 3-3-3 seat layout in Y class. Great leg room and seat wide 45 cm,with seat power supply and big IFE screen. Unfortunately IFE was average mostly arabic and bollywood films
New Boeing 777-300ER with 3-3-3 seating, wide seats with good leg room and recline with adjustable headrest. personal IFE, foldable table, tablet or mobile phone holder, USB port and outlet power.
A320Neo with comfortable seat and good leg room and recline with adjustable headrest, USB port and outlet power.

A320 NEO with new design and bigger overhead bins, seat new and comfortable. seat pitch on my seat (27H Aisle Seat) was 32 inch. Seat very comfortable. For travelling in Economy class on narrow body aircraft was a very great comfort.

I’m 6’6” 280 lbs, I sat in seat 14F on a flight from MCO Orlando to ALB Albany NY, legroom was awful, but I got to choose my seat unlike with southwest, slimline seats are not the worst but the seat back entertainment and free WiFi made up for legroom, it was sufficient for a 3 hour flight. Plus it’s JetBlue, they ranked lowest this year and I do not understand why, I checked in in less than 5 minutes at a kiosk in Orlando, no hidden fees, didn’t have bags so no extras and made it safe, how can you complain about JetBlue? There are far worse airlines in this country.

Extremely uncomfortable seat due to the sunken seat cushion and lack of lumbar support for a five hour flight from JFK to PHX. My spouse had the similar complaint. JetBlue used to offer one of the most comfortable seats. What happened?

JetBlue two weeks after I booked my tickets sent me an email that they moved my assigned seats as they claimed aircraft was changed. When I checked they took me out of my premium seats which I paid $147.00 and not only did not reimburse me but tried to charge me again when I tried to move my seats back. When I called the airline the JetBlue employee was not able to adjust the seats and had no idea what happened. I had to waste over 45 minutes on the phone after they called me back and still did not get the issue fully resolved. I booked 6 seats of which 2 were premium and they had no explanation as to why they moved all of our seats and why they moved everyone away from their travel companion.

JetBlue is my go-to airline. I last flew in May 2021 in my favourite seat, 7F with the wing and engine view on an Airbus A320 and the experience was perfect as always. The cabin was the new refreshed one and it was kept in a very clean state with all equipment in working order and the seats are nice and comfortable. The adjustable headrest is also a plus in terms of comfort. I am quite tall at 5ft 10 and the legroom can't be beat, even with my backpack under the seat in front of me, I had room to stretch out and relax and my legs didn't hurt. Excellent cabin service as always with kind and courteous flight attendants and entertainment options as well and power outlets are avaliable to charge your devices. The complimentary Wi-Fi was fast and I experienced no dropouts for the entire duration of my flight from MIA to EWR. I am flying on JetBlue again this August and I recommend this airline to anyone looking for a affordable airline with more comforts than even the legacy airlines such as American Airlines. I would also like to commend customer service for their help because when I was booking my latest flight, I somehow got two tickets when I am a solo traveller and they took care of the issue and I got credited back any points used after the site experienced issues when this occured and even was able to score my favourite seat for both my return and destination trips after this issue was corrected. This airline is truly top-notch in all fields.

JFK to Boston last night. I was in seat 4A and paid extra for that seat. The seat in front of me did not go into the upright position and was declared broken by the flight attendants. My tray table was also broken and would not hold a drink. It was hanging from the back of 3A. The staff did not seem concerned that upon landing and takeoff, Seat 3A was in my lap and not appropriate. This does not even sound like acceptable safety standards, much less worth the price I paid for a ticket. The plane and the seat was also filthy and there was debris/food/grunge around the screen in front of me. The seat I was in was dirty with I arrived and basically I expect at least cleanliness from the plane during COVID. I wanted a refund in compensation for the less than acceptable trip. I received 25$ CREDIT. I would avoid this airline at all costs. You get what you pay for. Cheap flights. Unfortunately, they are the only choice sometimes. I have many more issues with Jet Blue and really hope that in their race to grab a portion of international travel, their standards are quite higher. The web sight and receipts have minimal information and I had to request it. I could not access my flight into if I was not on line, which is most of the time when I travel. Their app is AWEFUL. I could not get a hold of anyone to talk to. Used a chat session that was mostly script. I have flown small planes in 3rd world countries that have better standards that Jet Blu. The flight attendant was also surly and unresponsive to my concerns. They get a 2 only because it was the end of a 28hr day of travel and they got me where I wanted to be on time.
A very uncomfortable seat in what looks like a new plane. No reclining seats, uncomfortable cushion. Do not use this airline if seat comfort is important to you.

Business class is just economy with an empty seat in the middle. At 188 cm tall, my knees hit the seat in front of me. When the passenger in front reclines the seat, it digs into my knees. And the flight is four hours. I don't recommend flying business class on this airline.

Horrible seat. No storage space beneath seat or overhead because another passenger put their bag up there. Very small labels to identify which is the correct seat and the cabin crew don't bother to give directions. No legroom, power sockets or entertainment. Wobbly tray table. Armrest was sticky and seat had droplets on it. At least I wore dark clothing to hide it rubbing off.

This review is for Warsaw to Chicago, Sept 5, 2023. Also, this is our first, and most likely last time we will fly on LOT. Positives: Very attentive and kind cabin crew. Plenty of beverages throughout the flight. Meals were somewhat basic (dinner and 'breakfast'), but adequate. Negatives: Very, very cramped. Not much space between rows, and even less when person in front of you reclines their seat. Given how little room there is, it is understandable that someone may want more space, but then there is no room to use your seat table. My wife had a drink on hers, which spilled when the person in front of her reclined their seat. If you drop something, good luck trying to find it while inflight. Aisles very narrow, barely any room to walk. For a 10+ hour flight, this is not a good choice.

Excellent pitch with plenty of space with good old-school quality comfortable reclining seats on an A330 . Same comfortable seating on my connect flight with B737 . My experience was very positive, following several previous trips with modern A320Neo's and A350/B787 and the seats with other airlines.

We got a great deal on the Premium Economy class RT to AMS and back. We picked the bulkhead window seats and the legroom was excellent. However, the legrest is rather useless as it does not offer any improvement on the seat. The food and service were above average and superior to economy but certainly nothing close to the business class as we upgraded to BC on the outbound flight. I will certainly recommend KLM and its PE and BC seats

Newer plane. Great seat arrangement 1-2-1. We had the middle seats. Seats were comfortable, lots of storage and plenty of space to work with and store in. Although no sliding doors for privacy, but the seats are situated in a way that not much is visible by the seat across the isle and vice versa. I will definitely recommend the KLM's 787 business class.

This is a standard, small aircraft used for by KLM Cityhopper short city connections within mainland Europe. The plane was clean and there is enough room in the aisle to board and move around. There is not much storage space in the overhead compartments because this is such a small plane. The seat is wide enough for a normal-sized person and there is enough distance to the seat in front. There is more space than in similar planes of KLM’s low-cost subsidiary Transavia. A free piece of pastry and a drink was served.

I travelled on 4 international flights with this airline on a recent trip. 3 were satisfactory. The 4th was a nightmare. The aisle widths and the seats have been reduced to accommodate more passengers. The seats are sublimely uncomfortable with pain in any position after about 15 minutes. I sat on the aisle and a large man sat in the middle who simply did not fit in the seat and encroached into my seat. I could choose to sit in contact with him from shoulder to knee or stick out in the aisle and be jostled by every passerby. It was a nightmarish flight overnight from Nairobi to Amsterdam. KLM obviously has no regard for its passengers to subject them to such torture and I will make every effort to avoid this airline in future.

Flew economy comfort, horrible seat, after six hours you do not know anymore to sit comfortable. After 10 hours you are completely broken and your back really hurts. No more cushion is provided by KLM in economy (comfort) class. This cushion could provide you with some support in lower back.

I booked seats 10J & 10K which are the front row in Economy Premium as I am 1.95m tall and I need the extra legroom. A few days before the flight I received a notice on my booking saying 'Due to operational reasons your seat has been moved to row 12". No other explanation and when I asked at the airport they could also not explain why the seat was changed. 12K is an appalling seat when you are tall and is not what one expects in premium economy at all. The seat was extremely narrow, cramped with minimal legroom. The two seats that I had booked were than randomly given to two young men (probably friends or relatives of KLM staff). The passenger in front of me kept his seat in full recline position and I could hardly move. He refused to put his seat up when I asked. The food was inedible with dry, thick sandwiches and unappetizing food. All min all this was an appalling experience and now I know why I changed from KLM to BA years ago - they change your seats at random for friends. I thought I would try it one more time but never again. I will be cancelling my return flight with a refund. The cost of the return flight for 2, with lounge access was NOK 31000 (US$4000). An outrageous price for nothing. Be warned

I booked a window seat on a KLM flight, seat A-18 on a Boeing 777-300ER. Little did I know that no Boeing 777-300ER on seat 18-A has a window, there is a wall. KLM is selling window seats where they know very well that because of aircodintioning reasons, there is never a window seat on 18A. What a scam! I am 1.90m tall and have a shoulder circumference of 132cm, So I need the window space to put 1 shoulder in which was impossible. So I had to steal 10cm of the middle passenger. That passenger was very unhappy during the 13,5h. When asking for a refund, KLM refuses.  KLM is not to be trusted anymore, stay away from them! I am waiting for a ticket refund of another €1.500 (flight of 04/05/20 cancelled on 29/03/20) already 210 days!
The Boeing 777-300 has absolutely the worse seating on an airplane. Their priority clearly is not passenger comfort. Tiny seats, no leg room! Avoid booking KLM at all cost!!

Uncomfortable seat for long-haul flight. Tasteless food. Hard working flight attendants who try to provide good service. Seat cushion is very thin over hard board underneath. Very uncomfortable lean-in to window. Leg room is sufficient. Audio-visual on seatback is totally unengaging. Music very limited, mediocre sound quality. While the flight attendants were quick to respond and courteous, a very uncomfortable seat that became nearly unbearable after 4 hours (16 hour flight) made the trip unacceptable quality. Terrible food , tiny quantities and no dessert. I would not recommend economy.

The back of the Boeing 747 has a lot of "yaw" in flight (side to side movement), which was uncomfortable. I don't think the middle sections of the cabin experienced this as much. Seat was not cushioned well and I was sore after a few hours. Inflight entertainment selection was lacking, and no free Wifi. OK legroom but not great. If you're in the middle seat, you have to wake somebody up to get out.

I flew with Lufthansa with the new cabin, called Allegris. There is so much more legroom, compared to normal economy seats, the screen is 13.3 inches with a very high quality 4k screen. On the screen there is a USB-A port, a USB-C port and the port for the headphones that they and out. A very nice thing is that you can connect your bluetooth headphones to the entertainment screen. You can connect to the wi-fi for free if you have a miles and more account, but the free part is only for messaging.The seats were much more reclinable. The food was really good, compared to a lot of other airlines; we had the classic choice of chicken or pasta. I chose chicken and it had a curry sauce on the side and vegetales. After that I watched a movie on the intertainment screen, where there were a lot of choices. After I finished the movie, I slept for 6 hours on a 9 hour flight from Chicago to Munich. Around 40 minutes before landing they gave us a snack. The landing was really good! It was a butter landing! The cameras were really on the plane on the entertainment screen were a very interesting thing, especially because there were cameras for all of the angles, from the tale of the plane, to the under of the plane; it was also on both sides of the plane, showing the engine and part of the wing. Overall, the flight was very smooth and comfortable, showing that Lufthansa really thought this thru.

Seat width and legroom is reduced to a minimum. If you are above 1.90m you won’t be able to fit in without touching the front seat, especially if the person in front of you lowers it to have a sleep. Same for your feet if you try to fit them below the front row. I almost had more space in my following short haul connecting flight with old A320. The table is ridiculously small. There is not enough space to store basic items with you : water bottle + phone + wallet and the seat pocket is overfilled. A detail compared to the seat comfort, but despite the plane being brand new, inflight entertainment system does not allow personal Bluetooth earphones connection.

LH A350-900 business class configuration is somewhat funny trying to give window access to all side seats; as a result, the individual cabins felt claustrophobic and surprisingly uncomfortable, both as seats and as beds. The seats are relatively narrow and barely long enough, which was all right for me but may be a real issue for bigger passengers.

The seat comfort in Lufthansa's short haul Business Class does not deserve the name Business Class. The seats are the same as in Economy and the seat pitch is also very low. Service and meals on board, however, were good.

While the staff, food and general communication with the airline through email and the app was really good both ways on my business class flights, the seats are like articulated coffins when you lie them flat. The planes seem to be older, I believe they are ex Philippine Airways. There is no mattress pad given to soften the sections in the seat as it moves to flatten out, so you are trying to lie on what feel like sideways slats - you can feel every single one! The area for your feet when the seat is flat is about a foot high and about 15 inches wide, so unless you only lie on your back there is no way to turn onto your sides. I fiddled around with the controls to see if I could get comfy for quite a while till I gave up, sat up, and leaned my head to sleep onto the shelf provided in the seat pod. It’s a terrible design and I had neck and back discomfort for two days post flight. Seats 7A and 7K. I was so disappointed as I had been looking forward to my flights for months. The good thing is that there is no one next to you and all the uneven numbered seats are right at the windows. Need to do better Lufthansa as otherwise I have no complaints.

The economy seats had barely any room between rows. If you were taller than 5'9" there was insufficient leg room. The entitled person in the seat in front decided to fully recline making a barely tolerable situation worse. When asked to limit the recline he responded that he needed to sleep. If seat room gets any closer, we'll be sharing seats or standing to fit more people on a plane. The tight connection from Vienna to Munich meant we had to jog to make our international flight, which is why our luggage is arriving tomorrow. Stewards were pleasant.

I purchased an extra space seat. Just before take off, the passenger seated next to me showed up with a very large dog. The dog was on leash but not in a container. I asked to be reseated but this was not possible as the plane was full. The dog continuously entered my space and disturbed my comfort; I had to constantly reposition my feet. I have asked for a refund but received various explanations regarding good will and liability but the answer remained no.

The seat and more particularly the seat layout is really disappointing for such a modern aircraft. The business class cabin looks as though it was designed 20 years ago. There's no aisle access from the window seats, whereas pretty much any other business class cabin in the 350 provides aisle access to all seats. More frustrating, there's absolutely nowhere to store anything. I really get the impression that Lufthansa chose the budget seat and cabin layout for their 350s. It's a shame as the soft product is excellent. Friendly staff, excellent catering.

Very bad service, the food was awful, the drink options were not good. No champagne for a business class. The seat is a joke, very tight and uncomfortable, even though it was one of the newest aircraft from the market. The checkin was the worst, I got a boarding pass that did not work, I couldn’t even get the digital one and no airport staff printed me a new one even I explained that was not working they haven’t reprinted it for me.

This seat is just not comfortable and my body was aching after a 2 hour flight from Munich to Catania. The only way to have a reasonably convenient flight in this seat is, when sitting in the first row. I reserved a first row seat and got a boarding pass for it but, when boarding was bumped backwards and had to squeeze into the limited space in the other rows in Business Class. Not a very nice feeling to be shown that it doesn’t really matter if one is loyal to Lufthansa. Like my last mid-distance flight on LHs A321 which even worse, I cannot recommend this aircraft for any flight other than very short haul, certainly not in business class and I definitely won’t pay the much higher price charged for this so called premium seat. But at least there was a USB charge point near the seat (in Evo and Business)

I fly Munich to Cairo and back and, unfortunately was booked on this about 4-hour overnight flight. Lufthansa still uses the A321 with standard short haul seats which just recline a few degrees and make it impossible to get some sleep. In business class, the middle seat is blocked by a table. This makes it impossible to use the free seat as an extension of the already too small seat. So, although there was nobody sitting next to me, I still had to cram into my horrible flimsy seat. It was just torture. In Economy, people could at least use the other seats to lay down if there is nobody sitting there. After arrival, I had to go straight to work which was difficult as I did not get a minute of rest.

During our return trip from Tokyo to Frankfurt we were assigned a seat in the lower deck of the business class section, which was broken, making the 11-hour and 40-minute flight extremely uncomfortable. When we brought this to the attention of the head flight attendant, she was apologetic, but did not offer any solution other than the manual manipulation of the seat, every time we needed to change its position. To our surprise, we found two members of what we believe was an orchestra seated in the upper deck of the business class section with their cellos strapped into chairs next to them. We feel that the head flight attendant could have easily asked one of them to switch seats with us, as the cellos would not have minded if their seat did not recline. Instead, we had to manually manipulate the seat every time we needed to change positions. Although the flight attendants offered to compensate us for the damaged seat, they changed their minds three times, stating that the compensation was only offered to European travelers, not Americans. Overall, I was extremely disappointed with the level of customer service on this flight, and afterward. For the high price of a business class ticket, I expected much better treatment and a more comfortable experience.

In my opinion, I think Lufthansa is a great airline, but their economy class could use some work. When I last flown with them the food in economy was absolutely horrendous. it was a very messy meal and at the end my stomach was aching. Also the seats were very cramped, and there was not even enough legroom to stretch out even for me who is 5ft9. All and all Lufthansa is great airline but if they fixed these points, they would have a lot more customers.

I have never been so uncomfortable for 11hrs. I'm 6ft tall and had almost no legroom. When the chair in front of me was reclined I had even less legroom and the joy of another chair basically in my lap which also made it very difficult to watch my low quality screen. This was flat out painful and I really don't recommend this for anyone.

I was extremely disappointed when I messaged customer service that the Business class seat I upgraded to did not lay flat for the 11 hour trip. I emailed them saying that the cabin crew tried their best but they were limited to what they can do and they were great about it. I requested for just a refund of the upgrade and their response was to offer a payment of 50 EUR.

One of the worst flights I have taken in recent years, I have flown Lufthansa before, and it was not like this before. The seats were so congested, the TV screen was too small and did not work, touch screen will not respond, extremely poor audio even with high quality headset. Food on our way was Ok, quality needs improvement, food service from Frankfort to Jordan was the worst, clod cheese sandwich. The flight from Cairo to Frankfurt, seats will not recline and so hard, sitting in those seats gives backpain. Frankfort to Houston, same A330, worst seating, recline won’t work, someone had to push up/down for recline to work, window seat is the worst, half of your leg space is taken by some aircraft equipment box.

Service was excellent. Food and beverage were also according to market level. The main problem here are the seats. It took Lufthansa forever to initiate the transition to newer business class seats. Despite the announcement of their new business class seats, who knows when we can finally experience it. Current seats do not match Lufthansa's pricing that skyrocketed and is I would say one of the worst in the premium segment. This is only compensated by the nice mileage program, service and staff.

Premium economy from Boston to Munich. Seat had good legroom, much better than economy at close to double the price. My main seat complaint is the fixed arm rest. My wife and I take 2 seats on the side on purpose but this strategy provides less room when the center arm rests are fixed. Entertainment system was good. I didn’t eat but food seemed economy-average. One point - the menu listed Warsteiner beer (a great beer) but they actually only had a skunked Beck;s (not a great beer). Also there was no amenity kit provided despite this being advertised. Overall a good, not great experience, potentially worth it for a 6’ tall passenger who can afford it. Not as good as some others.

This 17 inch seat and a 31" pitch for an international flight was horrible. I sat near the window and paid extra to pick the seat. I was in seat 18 at the window both to and from San Diego to Germany. If the seat number 16 in front of me had their seat back, I could not move. The passengers at the end of my 3 seat row, had extra leg room, but the carts kept running into them. If there was an emergency, I would have been stuck, because the seats are so close to the seats in front of them you cannot move past the other passengers in the row. The seats seam to be made of a polyester material that is slippery. When I would put my seat back and my legs reclined, I would slip down the seat. There was not way to sleep or be comfortable. If you fly an airline, whose economy seats are so small, it will be one of the worst flights of your life. Next time I will check the size of the seats.

Let me preface this review by saying that I'm 6'3, so I'm generally challenged for space in Economy, but despite the fact that 23C is an isle seat, this was definitely and positively the worst seat I've ever had the displeasure of occupying on an airplane. Already when the seat in front of me was still upright I was struggling to focus my eyes on the screen, because it was that close. When the seat in front of me reclined fully, I was literally unable to remain seated. I spent my time sitting on a pillow across the armrest with the legs in the isle, getting up when folks needed to pass, which is obviously not safe and not allowed. A kind flight attendant took pity on me and found a seat more suited for my anatomy. I can't imagine how horrible this 11 hour flight would have turned out to be, had it been completely full.

This flight from Philadelphia to Frankford was a little bit over eight hours so I upgraded to Lufthansa‘s premium economy. The row of seats right behind the last row in business has more legroom than other premium economy rows on the A330-300. The seat was very comfortable, plenty of storage, two windows, great entertainment.

The flight from Frankfurt to Oslo is only about 2 hours long and we of course know that seats have limited comfort and space. However, these seats and the space offered were considerably below our expectations. The seats are hard but the problem is the space which is very limited and feel cramped. Working with a laptop or eating is virtually impossible for a grown man who can only pray that the person in front is not recline their seat. It can be that the official figures show enough space but for all of us (we were 5 in the group), it was cramped and uncomfortable.
I flew Norwegian premium class from London to Ezeiza airport in Buenos Aires. The seat was comfortable and the entertainment system was great the only bad thing is the food.

I paid 90 AED for seat 1A, but the seat was stuck in a reclined position for the entire flight. I reported it to the flight attendant, but she said they couldn’t fix it. Although the crew was polite, it was disappointing to pay extra for a seat that wasn’t fully functional.

Premium economy seats were old Business Class type. Very old but happy to say my seat was slow but worked and went near flat. Comfortable and adjustable. No Power points NO entertainment so sleep or bring your own devices with plenty of power banks. No Air vents, No storage areas, just the floor or overhead bins. Table comes out from side rest - awkward and clumsy.

Comfortable seats with fairly good legspace compared to other low-cost airlines. There are no TV's or entertainment on board, nor are there any power supplies. The seats though are big enough and even though the seat in front of you reclines, you will not find a big difference in space.

Terrible and rock hard seats. It was a short to middle flight, but I think the seat could be a little bit more comfier. The crew service and onboard service was great, but the flight was very basic. No wifi and no onboard entertainment. When coming back home, I bought a larger seat, and it seemed to be a bit more comfier, but still uncomfortable.

Seat 9F - I am not a big fan of fake leather seats in hot climates. Luckily I don't wear shorts when I fly - pity those that do. Otherwise, the seat was clean, the tilt worked, but thankfully no one near me used it. The tray table was clean - although Not sure how clean - I wipe all surfaces anyway. Overhead bins are of decent size and with the new covid rules about checking oversized bags - there was plenty of room for legitimate hand luggage.

The seats are 2x2x2 in individual suite configuration. The seat width was very comfortable. Seats were lay-flat made of plush textile and well maintained. The inflight entertainment system was great and had a large selection of movies and TV shows.

Excellent seat in the sitting, lounge or sleeping position. Seat cover and pyjamas provided for sleep. Seats are in a forward Facing (as opposed to herring bone layout) with very generous (if not lavish) seat pitch. Oman Air provide great food together with warm and proactive service. In short an A1 business class experience.

Comfy leather covered economy seats. I was seated in row 17 which is over the wing; seats over the wings offer a quieter in-cabin experience. Seat 17A is a window, and mid cabin - so equal distance from forward and rear exit doors.
Worst seat in a Qantas International Business class product. 2x2 arrangement, old seat rather than one of the new seats. This seat hasnt changed in who knows how long.

QF7 - Sydney to Dallas - seats 37a & 37b - bulkhead behind seat. First time on Qantas premium economy, selected these seats as no interruption to recline with bulkhead behind. Very nice seats and good sized entertainment screen. Power options available. Great additional storage along window side, very handy. Didn't seem to be any issue for recline from the other premium seats. Very happy with seating choice - recommend.

In September we took our first Business Class flight for a couple of years returning from Samoa on QF340. With a flight time of 6.5 hrs and late arrival into Sydney, we were looking forward to the extra comfort and service. We had seats 5E & 5F located next to each other in the center of the aircraft. The seat design is an insult to passengers travelling together, the idiot who designed these seats has no idea about the needs of travelling companions. You are separated by a fixed “divider” making it almost impossible to see each other and have any form of conversation. My wife is an anxious flyer due to an experience with an emergency landing which almost had a fatal outcome for all on board. Being separated like this made it very difficult for her, I spent half the flight on the edge of my seat leaning around the “divider” so I could talk to and console my wife who was stressed throughout the flight, very uncomfortable. Economy Class would have been so much better. There was no welcome drink or an amenities kit – where has the Qantas standard gone! For dinner we were served roast chicken that was inedible, tough and chewy! No entrée and the little dessert cake came in a paper box. After eating half of the dessert, I stopped due to a piece of the paper lining coming free and ending up in my mouth – disgusting! My wife didn’t touch her dessert. Why are we paying extra for this rubbish, had better meals in economy. While the seat and food proved to be a huge disappointment, the staff were very friendly and attentive. Being a “gold for life” Frequent Flyer, I have experienced many O/S business class flights over the past 25 years but this was the worst, never again – Qantas has totally lost the plot!! When we go to Europe next year, it will be on another airline.

They changed the aircraft from an A330 to a 737-800 and the seats must have been for short haul flights of two hours or less, as the 5 hour and 40 minute flight I endured was on the most uncomfortable seats I have experienced. The other story is trying to get a refund for the seat location we paid for, but we’re bumped from after they changed the plane type.

Seat 26 H and K. These are the only 2 seaters available on the plane. Very useful for couples. Acres of legroom is another plus factor. Downsides are lack of window and proximity to toilet and the queues for them at certain times.

I hate to say it but this would have to be the worst Business Class offering I have flown in over 20years. The seats we were allocated in row 2, and were barley even a decent premium economy seat. They were tight uncomfortable and cramped. My wife who had the window seat said it felt like she was trapped in a box. The amount of space allocated for these two seats is appalling. There was no storage whatsoever, not even to rest a drink bottle. Never again.

The massage function on this seat did not seem to work well, felt hardly any movement. It was very comfortable whilst seated upright. Once the seat was reclined, and the foot well was very tight. I did not have a good night. A full breakfast was offered after take-off (almost midnight Sydney time). Strangely not many passengers accepted. Prior to landing a light meal was offered. I was asked every time I used the toilets whether I was a business class passenger. The paper towels in the bathroom were so thin it dissolved in wet hands. The lounge was Premium Plaza Lounge and I would not pay good money to use it. Food was limited, the pasta was congealed and the cakes/desserts was dry from sitting too long on display.

The design are beautiful with a great choice of colour. The seats are bit harder compare to the old seat but its slim design make leg room more spacious. The are no IFE but the are phone slot to replace IFE. For me, the seat comfort was moderate but suitable for my 2 hours journey flight.
The seat was good and comfortable enough for 6 hours flight. The width is big enough for my body. The legroom is modest. Adjustable headrest well function. Lucky enough to occupy all three seats.

IFE inconsistent and poor - if you end up flying on one of MAS' 737-800s that have not been refurbished or retrofitted for some reason, despite having a core fleet of 737-800 for a long time now, there won't be any inseat IFEs, even in business class. If you do get to board a "standard" 737-800, you'll find the IFE rather outdated and tedious to use, compared to other similar airlines. Endless clicking and scrolling just to look for movies/music/shows - very poor user interface and leads to passengers spending too much time holding the remote, which is not ideal given the current situation. Flight Info function was not working at all on one flight, which was inconvenient.

Seat was decent and clean, the legroom and seat width is sufficient. But one thing that annoys me is the seat recline not functioning. The economy class cabin needs refurbishment because it is still the same cabin I have been a few years ago. The seat does not have a headrest. The IFE system is decent but outdated although the entertainment content is still up to date. The interface needs a new look, including the system and console itself.

Fantastic flight with Qatar Airways, the best I have flown. We were in economy class, but paid for an extra legroom seat. We were in a part of the aircraft with only 3 rows for a total of 24 seats, all with the same characteristics: a kind of Premium Economy. Due to the 2x4x2 configuration, the seats were very wide with enormous legroom and a very reclining backrest. I tried the Premium Economy of Singapore Airlines, but this flight of Qatar was much superior in terms of comfort.

The Qsuite seat was terrific with lots of privacy and wonderful amenities. IFE, blanket, pillows and food were all excellent. Seat comfort for sitting or sleeping is great. Unparalleled service as well.
Spacious, clean and comfortable seat with outstanding IFE and food served. Excellent amenities and blankets/pillows. Qsuite with privacy and lots of legroom with easy to use seat controls.
Wide and comfortable with enough legroom. Clean, perfect level of recline. Headphone and control point on the seat. Seat covers were good and clean, looked new and properly maintained.
