Pleasant cabin layout. The screen size was excellent and the provision of power supply is also commendable. Good seat, legroom good enough for me, good recline and seat width also, access way is enough.
I booked Qsuites and I got a 2x2x2 cabin configuration with angled bed, one of the worst trips of my life.
Wide and comfortable with enough legroom. Clean, perfect level of recline. Headphone and control point on the seat. Seat covers were good and clean, looked new and properly maintained

Brilliant service and facilities. The QSuites product is best in class and has set a very high bar. Food and beverage excellent, quality top notch. Al Mourjan lounge definitely one of best business class lounges in the world.

I opted for a regular economy seat on the Mumbai-Doha leg of the flight and a preferred seat on the Doha-Chicago leg. Unfortunately the seats were disappointing and uncomfortable. Lumbar support was poor, my leg space was compromised with IFE boxes intruding into he foot well which made the Doha -Chicago leg really uncomfortable. There were only USB charging points on the seat.

This was a very nice experience. The steward was extremely friendly and attentive. The seat was roomy, comfortable and had it own sliding door for privacy. The food was delicious and service impeccable. As this was an overnight flight, whilst changing into the complementary pajamas, the flight attendant prepared my bed, with mattress and pillow case. Altogether, this was a perfect experience.

Recently, I reviewed a Business Class seat on an A350-900 whilst on a flight from BER to DOH. Today, I ended up on the same aircraft, but with a different seat layout. I reserved a window seat, but during checkin, I was just assigned a different seat in the middle bit of the row. I tried to change this at the airport, but was told, that it’s not possible. So, no QSuite, but a middle seat with a small divider to my neighbor. There was no privacy, the seat felt stuffy, there was not much legroom. Not a nice experience.

This is a QSuite seat. The seat is very roomy and ergonomically arranged. Storage is sufficient and the sliding door gives enough privacy. If one travels with a partner, the middle divider can be lowered, making this a private 2-person Suite. The seat is very well suited for a long night on a plane. One of the best seats I’ve travelled in.

We went from Berlin to Doha in Business Class. The seats were clean and comfortable but felt a bit small. Every seat was equipped with its own sliding door. The seat was not one of QR’s famous QSuite seats. There was an Iphone holder with integrated charger which I found very useful. The socket was not working properly. There was not a lot of storage room, so I had to put my shoes in the overhead compartment. All together, this was a pleasant flight which felt a bit “corporate”.

Pleasant cabin layout. Good chair. But avoid row 34 since that's the row without one of these great 787 windows. No info at booking, so take care if you like a seat with a view. Seating quality is ok.

I had a very comfortable seat (17C) with extra room for my legs, as there is no seat in front. However, if you prefer having a possibility to stow small things in a seat or wall pocket during your flight, that seat might not be for you, as there is none. Also your screen is retractable, which means you can’t use it during takeoff or landing. However, with a tablet, you fine (besides not being able to stow it).
Q Suite (seat 1A) The best seat type in Business class, in terms of comfort and sleeping in. The flight attendants prepare your bed with a bed mattress, extra pillow and you get pajamas.

This review refers to the Q suite, it really one of the very best in flying and luxury experience. It is almost like flying first class for the price of business. Try it for yourself if you can, you will see what I mean.
Seat has a good legroom. The screen size was excellent and the provision of power supply is also commendable.

The service was extremely good and I like to personally name the crew on board who performed this service on flight QR 274 on the 16th of April 2021 from Amsterdam to Doha, thank you very much: Faishal, Rudy, Prudence and Lynda, it was a joy flying with you.
Good seat, legroom good enough for me, good recline and seat width also, access way is enough, tv screen enough with good entertainment.
Seats in economy are quite comfortable, I could strech my legs , more or less (I am 180 cm). Space between seats is good. Very comfortable seats and very good reclining.

A319LR seat very comfortable, it is possible to lay down to horizontal. Easy handling. Good space for even larger peoples. A elder airplane with this new high class seat, this is special. Boeing 787-8 very comfortable, a full bed. Highly comfortable for long haul flights. No difference between this two aircraft seats!

Philippine Airlines adds one more seat in the row in Economy class which gives a seat configuration of 3-3-3. A configuration found in aircraft with a wider cabin. A330 are usually configured 2 - 4 -2. In addition the seat distance is made for locals. I am 183cm and my knees touched the seat in front. There are charging ports for the phone but they did not work. There is no Inflight Entertainment Screen or connection for a headphone. On the seat is written that there is WIFI but it did not work.

Row 41 on the A321 is a very comfortable seat, however I did have to pay a premium for the upgrade. Not sure what airlines are doing these days, but there appears to be very little lumbar support on these seats. Fortunately nobody was sitting next to me, so I was able to pad things out with a few pillows that were not in use. Saved me from any discomfort for that seven hours of flight, but I'm sure that I could not have stood much more than that.

Flew PR119 flight from Toronto to Manila, 16-hours of uncomfortable sitting in a Business Class seat. The seat buttons did not function so the seat was immovable, finishing the journey with a neck pain and sore back. The inflight Chief Purser stated that this is an ongoing issue with the airline and the airline isn't rectifying it.

The monitor in seat 68B would randomly shut off and the headphone jack was broken, this is very disappointing especially on a long flight; I had the same problem the last time I flew with them, why can't they fix their electronics? When returning on September 25th PR117 my selected seat was changed, I was told there was nothing they could do. I selected a window seat; why couldn't they accommodate me with a similar seat? They were extremely reluctant to help, they just kept saying that they reserve the right to switch the seats.

We (2 passengers) had both a horrible experience with our seats deflating, so that we had a horizontal metal bar pushing hard against out mid thoracic spine on this 16 hour flight! Exactly the same happened on the return leg on different business class seat allocations. Each time the crew was trying hard to improve the situation with blankets, but it was still a painful experience. Business class was full, so no option to move seats. During the stopover in Vancouver a technical crew came on board, attended to my seat and showed me how to take the seat cover off and manually blow air into the seat with my mouth), which I had to do 3 times during the flight back from JFK after Vancouver. The business class seat is actually a really good product (on A350-900, same like Qantas) with air cushioned seat that should be adjustable, but the airline simply doesn’t maintain or repair it. It is such a shame, but it reflects the overall chaotic operation of this airline. On boarding the MEL-MNL (different business seats) leg I immediately noticed that my remote control was broken with exposed wires and it is only after I insisted that they put a sticker over the wires to conceal them (the plane was still on the ground in Melbourne). Seat on the MEL-MNL-MEL ok, but tiny footwells (A330-300). During each transit in Manila we had to wait for our suitcases to be found and open them for security inspection, almost missing our return flight back to Melbourne because they had difficulty finding our luggage. That is a normal procedure, when transiting in Manila. I’m not going to even go into the catering, other than to say that “they are trying”. IFE was mediocre. I have not received an answer to my complaint, despite repeated emails. To sum it up: Horrible airline, zero customer service! While the tickets seem cheaper compared to other airlines, they are in fact terrible value for money…

The A321-200 neo seat has enough legroom that passengers seated in the aisle seat need not get up when passengers in the middle or window side want to get up. It has its own TV monitor and enough compartment. What’s lacking is the charger. The fabric is also comfortable and perfect with its blue color.
Flight on Airbus 320. The cabin was a little worn off but clean, seat itself was okay. Not very comfortable but okay for a short flight. Bathroom was clean.
What business class? There is none. Same seats and same cabin and same toilets. Like economy. The seats so small and with less cushion that it was painful for a 5 hour flight.

I paid a premium to get leg room and all I got was a cattle class seat with my knees wedged into the back of the seat in front and a "free" meal in a cardboard box. One expensive meal that was! There was not even an empty seat in row 3, which is usually the case when using the front of the plane for premium. Just my wife, myself, and a stranger, crammed into three narrow seats. There were none of the other onboard courtesies normally afforded premium passengers, such a priority boarding or deplaning. The crew were pleasant enough, though nothing outstanding. There were WiFi connection cards in the seat pockets, but the plane was old and had no WiFi We did enjoy access to the lounge. Given CPH is one of SAS's home ports the lounge was far from resplendent. The food selection was minimal, nothing typically Scandinavian. Soup, salad, one beer, coffee, no deserts. I had to wait 10 minutes for a young man to stop fiddling in the kitchen and bring me a soup spoon.

Unbelievably disappointed. So long as this seat design exists I will never travel with SAS again. I buy premium economy seats when I travel with family. I’ve flown on dozens of different airlines all over the world. I don’t buy business on family trips because of one very specific reason, the lift up hand rests. The ability to open up horizontal space and snuggle with my significant other is essential. These seats suck. They are as narrow as domestic economy, and they have massive thick metal barriers between each seat that cram you in. This is hands down the most uncomfortable seat I’ve flown on in years. What a joke.
I‘m very satisfied with the latest slimline seat at SAS. It feels more comfortable than Lufthansa‘s and has a better legroom. All of them have an USB-Port, seat pockets and a large tray table.

Seats are too small for a 6 hours service. This was the worst seat experience I have had. Normally, they can use seats like this for a 1 hour flight, but it's very shocking to use this configuration for a long journey. No seat recline, no individual tv set for a 6 hour flight. No power socket to charge phone for a 6 hour flight.

This was my 3rd roundtrip ticket with Saudia in the past 2 yrs, the previous flights were reasonable for the price paid, but these last 2 flights were very bad. I flew MNL - RUH - CDG. On the first flight from MNL I had booked seat 70L. Heard the crew saying: Are we ready for the movie marathon, while handing out the earplugs, or is it gonna be a sleeping marathon? Well, quickly most passengers found out the last would apply, because more then 75% of the screens didn't work. Sleeping for me was also not an option, because the recline also didn't function.  This B777 was in a real bad shape. The cabin crew member did give me another seat in the front of this cabin, but with the 3x4x3, try to eat all at the same time, rubbing elbows? There was nothing comfortable about this flight.  The flight to CDG, also a B777, but not much better then the flight from MNL. Here also most screens of the entertainment system didn't work and the USB ports also didn't function.
Very comfortable seats with ample legs room. Foot rest was helpful for long flight. Food was served with napkins for food trays. Overall I find seating arrangement very good.

In addition to the Long Haul and Untra Long Haul versions, Singapore Airlines operates a medium hall version of the A350 and that is by far my favourite. It offers the choice of either a left- or right-hand side consol. The seat configuration is 1-2-1 staggered. Each offers direct aisle access but for single seats with extra privacy choose A or K - 12, 15, 17, or 20. What makes these seats so great is they can be converted from upright to fully flatbed (and everything in between) with the push of a button. Unlike the other A350’s and 777’s with the crazy ‘flip’ seats that force you to sleep in a strange and uncomfortable angle. Regardless of where you sit, the seat offers a curved privacy wing with built in angle light options for reading. The 18″ screen provides access to the KrisWorld system which is loaded with movies, TV box seats, games and audio. You can control it by a touchscreen or use the remote which makes it easier to control the system while lying down. There is an AC power point and two high-speed USB charging ports in the console plus Business Class passengers can enjoy free Wi-Fi. There’s a blanket, large pillow, pair of slippers, eyeshades and a bottle of water at each seat. However, your unlikely to find an amenity kit, but these are available on demand.

We recently travelled Auckland - Singapore -London - Singapore - Auckland, on both the A350 and B777. Service was perfect, as usual, and food quality was generally good.Entertainment seems to have declined. The great disappointment was the Business Class seat, same on both aircraft. It cannot be fully reclined without conversion to a bed, and to put your feet up requires twisting diagonally into a barely comfortable position. Not much better when fully flat in bed form. I have travelled on Singapore business and first over almost 30 years, and this seat is the worst i have experienced.

Singapore Airlines have been updating their long-standing light-brown coloured economy seats with newer blue coloured seats. Whilst the inflight entertainment tech has certainly benefited, SQ have made a shocking choice of seat type / pitch. SQ state that these seats have a 32 inch pitch. I am definitely taller than average 6'8", but did fit in their previous economy seats. This is no longer the case. Whether it's due to the cushion thickness, design method of seat recline etc, the simple fact is that SQ's newer economy seats are far more cramped and uncomfortable. The SQ service remains good, but this doesn't really matter when you simply can't fit into their seats and experience genuine discomfort on long-haul flights. I experienced this issue on both their A350-900 and A380. In my opinion, when travelling long-haul, being in a seat with legroom and being comfortable, are the most important factors in choosing which airline to use next.

Like the majority of their regular business class passengers I hate the business class seats on their A380 aircraft. The seat and surrounding environment are great for take-off, landing or whenever in the normal seated position. But when it comes time to sleep, then good luck with that one. It soon becomes the most uncomfortable business class lay flat bed in the sky. What were they thinking? Well clearly, they were not.  At least they are more likely to get a decent night’s sleep that the poor passengers trying to get comfortable on this seat. Please Singapore Airlines – do something to address this issue. Given these aircraft are most likely going to be around for a lot longer that initially planned, don’t make your loyal customers continue to suffer. At least get some decent bedding.

A major fatal flaw in the terribly designed business class seat which is truly awful if you want to try to sleep! While it’s a flat bed you are forced to sleep diagonally with very narrow footwells so that if you want to change position to lie on your side then your other side it’s impossible! It’s to restrictive to move so you’ll hardly get any decent sleep unless you have consumed large amounts of alcohol from the great choice on the wine list - whoever designed this seat needs to be fired! Apparently talking to one flight attendant they did say there’s a refit of new seats & interior on this aircraft planned but wasn’t sure when. Seat adjustment controls worked if you hold & press, which is a bit outdated & needs improvement. lighting was sufficient for reading. Privacy on an aisle seat is never any good so if that’s what you want then window seat is recommended. So A380-800 business class seat not recommended & if you want a good nights sleep & opt for the A350 or 777 aircraft with Singapore.

We were in seats 33A and 33C - would highly recommend these seats as they are the last seats in premium economy section with a bulkhead behind which allows you to have the seat reclined whenever you like without interfering with passengers behind you. The first row seats in premium economy s 31 similarly have no seating in front as on exit row but TV screens are either mounted in between the seats in a centre console or on the bulkhead in front, excellent legroom but screen position could be an issue.

I had confirmed the seat suitable for my needs, had the seat confirmed with the boarding pass printed and issued to me. At the point of boarding I was told my seat was moved with no real reason given although we suspect it was to accommodate other passengers who do not seem to have any real reason to need to take over my seat. I ended up having to sit with the bad ear nearer to the aisle and could not hear what the flight attendant was saying. I am most displeased at this inconsiderate change without any prior discussion with me by the airline.

This seat is cramped. The pitch is 30-31 inches. The metal support from floor for seat in front is exactly in the space where you would naturally place your right leg, reducing the legroom significantly. I could not imagine siting in this seat for 12 hours, it would be torture. Luckily for me was a quick trip to Bangkok.

The most uncomfortable seat encountered. Minimal padding, no lumbar support, extremely uncomfortable, for the 6 hour flight to Cairns from Singapore. Don't book, unless you want to be in extreme discomfort, and have back ache for a day or two after. I am 6 ft tall, slim and fit. I booked an exit row seat thinking it would be more comfortable, but the seat has a stub as an arm rest meaning it is about 13 inches wide in practice.

I tried the new A388 business class from London to Singapore. It was about 12-13 hours. My seat was 21K on the upper deck, along with the suites (the old ones used to be in the bottom deck). I think that the seat was pretty spacious for me (I'm 164cm) the footrest was good, but the legroom was to either to your left or right, which makes it quite uncomfortable. But on the SQ regional J class, its a straight legroom, so consider getting a 787-10/359 if you want a straight legroom. The bed couldn't recline fully into a flat bed, unlike the 773,359, the 388 uses buttons to recline the bed, it is done automatically, while the 773/359 is done manually. The table was pretty small compared to the 773/359 (hard to get out of your seat while the table is open) and some tables are also not fully functional, like mine, during landing the table popped back out, I have tried several times to push the table back in, but it just won't fully go in, it would still be loose. The crew was very kind, friendly and welcoming. They kept checking on me, which made me feel weird but happy in a way. I had 2 meals in total on this flight, lunch and supper/dinner. The lunch wasn't my favourite, the scrambled eggs were pretty basic. But the Dinner/supper, I love it, it was steak beef served with mash potatoes and a couple of vegetables, (not book the cook).

Chose a window seat so I could lean against the pillow and window as I usually do. But due to large gap between seat and arm ready window side it was very uncomfortable. Leg room minimal. I’m 5,5 . It seems new but not well designed. Tray table not adjustable and too close to body.

Worst business class seat I’ve ever had. Very thin cushioning, not comfortable. Bed cover is not a mattress at all, just a thin piece of material. You can’t lie straight, you have to lie on an angle and rest your legs on the footrest with your feet in a small cavity. Very poor for a business class product, Avoid at all costs.

Not really comfortable chair or bed. Singapore Airlines offer a proper bed and a separate chair in First Suite: Both are rather disappointing, especially taken into account the huge investment and Publicity. The leather chair stands alone in the middle of the Suite, one has to move it from the take-off position, to the dining position, and to the outside view position. The bed is not facing the direction of travel, but crossways in the suite. The bed is narrow and very hard, not very comfortable. When the bed is not used, it hangs across the suite like a chunk of white painted wood. The whole design is not well thought through and not nicely done.

Worst business class seat I have experienced Automatic seat controls did not work on either the outbound or return flight, so flight attendant assistance was required several times. Same with the center wall divider partition that required attendant assistance to lock it in place for both flights. Seat design requires you to lie at an angle in order to use the foot rest space. Overall, was not impressed with this business class product &amp.

The 3x3x3 configuration on the A350-900 is desperately cramped. I have short legs but my knees were knocking against the seat in front and the 6 flights comprising my journey from London to Perth and return were spent with a neighbour's elbow poking into my side because of the narrowness of the seat and the armrest. Hard seats compounded the problem. No refresher towels or overnight comfort packs except a skimpy one on the outward leg on SA. Minimal food choice, and what was provided to me was inedible apart.
My seat (71J) was terrible. There was 2 black boxes fixed under the seat before me leaving me only 60% of the space that my feet would have had if I had been sitting in different row.

Seating is very uncomfortable.  Sleeping configuration is not comfortable. You need to sleep on an angle sticking your feet in a small hole. The seat is lightly padded. Food is low quality for business class and no longer offers a rich Peranakan mix, but a Chinese bias. Media system resets when any connected device detaches and reattaches. Book the chef food never got loaded.

Headrest is fixed and not changeable. Armrest are 2 small foldable tables.  IFE Flightinfo can not save changes to metric system by each change to movie or music an return to flight info. Touchbuttons to change the seat not working (crew needs to change the seat to bed). Bed is not to sleep for passengers who sleep on sides. Hole for feet is to small for footsize 46.

Boeing 787-10 leg room was adequate, it shouldn’t be a worry for medium-haul flights like this (SQ878). The screen size was good, it was difficult for you and your neighbor to see each other’s screens, giving you a decent amount of privacy. The 3-3-3 configuration makes it easy to access the aisles (with the exception of window seats) compared to most other wide body airliner. Power sockets are available to keep your devices charged. A cup holder is also present which was a nice touch as you no longer need to worry about your drink spilling over and onto your seat.

The Boeing 787-10 legroom is fine, but the seat feels very narrow and is uncomfortable. The A350 seats which I flew earlier were much better. Not sure if I would want to fly on Singapore Airlines Boeing 787 again.

We flew Singapore to LAX Premium Economy and were completely disappointed. The seats had recline and footrests alright but were so narrow we were both very uncomfortable all night. Food was awful (stale buns) Eg Pasta shrimp salad had no dressing, vegetables were stewed beyond recognition . Service was brusque to the point of being rude. Icecream tub was almost thrown at me in the haste to get service done quickly . No welcome drink. Requests for water were forgotten. We have in the past had the pleasure of travelling premium economy Air NZ and there is NO comparison. Don’t know what happened to Singapore Airlines supposed excellence for service. Their Premium Economy offering was fairly price competitive (albeit our first leg from Australia was only offered in economy), however I think they make this happen by essentially providing economy level meals (No amenities pack ). The poor service is a total shock. Have they lost their mojo?
The seats were hard and didn't recline. Very uncomfortable. It gave me a terrible back pain. It is amazing how airlines try to maximize profit at the expense of comfort and health.

The Big Seat!  I was flying to New Orleans for a conference and splurged for the Big Seat. It was the longest flight I had ever taken with Spirit. Everyone I think knows you can only last a few hours in a regular economy seat. Well, at first when I sat down in the Big Seat, the bottom half of the seat sagged and left an uncomfortable gap between the bottom and back rest. I just overlooked that and just hoped for the best. After all the seats do have a leather pillow added to the head rest for extra comfort, wrong! About 20 minutes of leaning my head on this, I started to feel some pain in my neck. It was really hard to get comfortable after this point and the pain in the back of my neck turned into a cramp like feeling. The only way I could get comfortable was to slide my head off the sewn in pillow so my head was more inline with the rest of my body. Turns out the pillow was extending my head forward so much that it was causing neck cramps. So my experience with paying extra for this supposedly upgraded seat turned out to be a total dud. It may be ok for some people but the comforts of upgrading to the Big Seat is not for me or everyone. Will be sticking to exit row seats and shorter flights under 3 for this airline.

For this particular trip back home to Philadelphia from Las Vegas I upgraded to the Big Front Seat. The flight was a little bit over five hours and it was better from my original flight to Las Vegas on a regular seat. I find that the older models have a more comfortable Big Front Seat with more legroom. Although the new airplanes look and feel great, there is an overall issue with comfort and you still feel cramped in, even in row 1. I have made the decision not to fly Spirit on flights longer than 3 hours. Sadly their product is not designed for longer than that.

I was very excited to fly on this brand new configuration of the A320 Neo. We all know Spirit crams you in and for this particular flight I was on the middle seat, luckily for me I was traveling with two family members so we had the entire row and it was not that uncomfortable sitting in the middle because on each side I had family rather than strangers. This was supposed to be a five hour flight from Philadelphia to Las Vegas that turned into a seven hour flight due to taxi delays at takeoff and once we landed. Those seats by no means are designed to be seated on for more than 4 hour maximum. I am 5’9” 150lbs so it was not a matter of not fitting in the chair but a matter of virtually no padding. Your lower back and legs begin to get num after 3 hours sitting on pretty much a plastic seat. Not sure Spirit will improve this but be aware that unless you can afford to upgrade to a Big Front Seat it will be brutal to fly on a regular seat for more than 3 hours. Heading back to Philly I’ve already secured a Big Front Seat so look out for that review. Like I do on all my Spirit Airline reviews, they do not claim to be the most comfortable or service orientated airline. They take you from point A to point B safely and for this flight they did just that.

Spirits new improved seats are not designed to fit most people comfortably. It took the rest of the day for my back and neck to feel normal. Forget sleeping, and sitting is barely tolerable. I will never fly Spirit economy again. I am giving a 1 because the program won't let me rate this a zero

The seats did not recline in any way and if you're a larger than a teenager you have absolutely no room to move in those seats there is no in-flight entertainment no comfortability if you suffer from restless leg syndrome do not fly with them you have no room to adjust your legs your knees are basically touching the seat in front of you.

I usually flew them on the LGW-ATH and ATH-LGW route and I did so on a repeat basis. They served this route with a A321 but they switched aircraft last minute. Their aircraft  are extremely tight legroom wise but I flew them on the basis that I prebuy extra legroom seats in an exit row which cost 25 euros. They advertised the seats on row 12 as exit row and extra legroom. However, on 3 occasions, they changed their aircraft to a A320 for operational reasons and reseated me in seats which cost the same but were not extra legroom. The first two occasions I called their customer service and I was able to reseat myself in a row with extra legroom. In the third occasion, for which I am submitting this review, they changed the aircraft to an A320, reseated me to 4F, which is not extra legroom. They did not notify me beforehand and did not provide me any options. I found out at checkin. I called their customer service before departure and I explained that I could not fly with their limited legroom and requested that they change my seat. They were not able to accomodate me as the plane was full. I said I could not fly in this case and I explained I wanted resolution to the matter before takeoff so that they dont deem my absence as a no show. They did not offer to change my date or do anything. They instead told me to email them with the circumstances implying I could get my money back. When I emailed them, I did not receive a response for a month. They ignored me. When I pestered them again, I received a response that this was a "no show" and I could not be reimbursed except for taxes and as a favor for the seat charge. They advertise seats as extra legroom and change them without having explicitly rules about doing that. They have since changed the indication "extra legroom" in those seat but have left it in when you click in it (see attachment). Second, they did not notify me in time and give me options. Third, I called to make changes before departures but they led me to believe that I would be reimbursed instead of telling me that I would be losing my money as a no show (I probbed them on this matter). This level of service is not acceptable.

Seat 12F. This was a great seat for the price paid for my ticket (£24). I chose random allocation so I didn't pay for the seat. I was given 12E (the middle seat - a classic Ryanair punishment for not paying for a seat, but the 12F passenger didn't show up so I moved. I had a small under seat bag, and still had plenty of legroom.
Seat 26A. This was a randomly allocated seat, and in terms of the view, behind the wing on the port side (left) of the plane. Good view and good legroom for the price paid.

Booked extra legroom seats for me and my partner, especially since usual seat layout is well too cramped for a 6'2" man. Was allocated 1B and 1C which was fine. Except priority boarding which came with the allocation was nonsensical since everyone and his dog has to file past us to reach their seats. Plus the cabin crew seats are directly opposite and they're not comfortable either so my leg room got totally compromised during take off and landing, and by their backwards and forwards servicing all the other passengers during the entire flight. The two seats need to be positioned closer to the aircraft side to provide non-contact by the food, beverages, and duty free trollies - or else what's the point of paying for extra leg room? The crew were very polite but that didn't make up for a very uncomfortable flight when comfort was the very thing we paid extra money for. Budget should never mean discomfort.

The seat was unusually thin, the coating of it felt like fabricated plastic. The seat did not recline nor did it have a moveable head rest. Fortunately, the leg room was pretty decent. There was enough room to put my backpack under the seat. The seat is comfortable for the first 2 or 3 hours of the flight, however after that it becomes very uncomfortable. Good enough for a budget airline though!

The seat is bolt upright, with no adjustment or storage. While a seat like this might be suitable for ultra short haul it is not suitable for a flight of four hours. Very uncomfortable seat, it must be the worst in class. It deserves a zero rating.

Small legroom like most European airlines, but not that bad for tall people, this is because although the legroom is small, the seats don't recline, and for tall people, at least for me is a big plus, because once the seats in front of you recline, the legroom is completely gone. With Ryanair you are guaranteed that the person in front if you will not recline the seat, and since Ryanair trips are not long haul, I'd say its a good compromise for tall people.

I hadn't flown for quite a few years, and this trip to Jamaica and back was the worst experience for seating I have ever had. To have to upgrade to board first is ridiculous. We were in group C with grab any seat that is left splitting up your party. With that said there is no managing of the seat arrangements. So with 3 seats on each side, couples will take the isle seat and window seat with their carry on's in the center seat and not willing to give it up. My daughter had to argue with a man on the plane about it. Fortunately his girlfriend moved to the center seat. There were other unhappy people that ran into the same situation. The open seating is fine but needs to be managed better. If at all possible I will NEVER fly this air line again. At least assigned seating you knew you had a seat and didn't have to grapple for one, AND majority of the time you wouldn't be splitting up the party you are with. Very unhappy about this part of my trip!

The seat is 54 cm wide, but once converted into a bed, it expands to 62 cm, offering enough space to lie flat and sleep without feeling restricted. The bedding provided — including a mattress topper, duvet, and pillow — was high quality and made the bed genuinely comfortable. The layout feels private, thanks to the suite-style design. While the sliding partition isn’t full height, it gives a good sense of separation. There’s a generous amount of room around you, and the design is stylish but understated. There’s a large 32-inch screen right in front of the seat. The screen resolution was sharp, and the sound system came with noise-cancelling headphones. Storage space was enough for personal items. The table is large and stable. The seat controls were simple to use, and it was easy to find the perfect position for sitting, lounging, or sleeping. Cabin crew were attentive and respectful, always nearby without being intrusive.

We paid $92 USD for extra legroom, which granted us barely more than the cheapest seats on Delta airlines. As long as you place backpacks and other under seat items in the overhead bins, you may have enough space to stretch your legs straight forward in front of you. The seats are nearly wide enough for a person wearing a US man's medium to fit, barely. They're hard, like folding wooden chairs, with little padding and forcing you to sit at an angle that pinches the sciatic nerve, even when reclined. When the person in front of you reclines, the TV is extremely close to your eyes and there's no room to get up at all. The aisles are so skinny, walking up and down them for relief is not an option, unless you walk sideways. The staff bump the carts along all of the seats up and down the aisles, so you have to sit with your arms crossed and shoulders pulled in, which causes pain in the back and neck.

The worst business class seats we have experienced among the ones we have flown so far (UA, AA, ITA, AF, BA and KLM). Congested cabin, a 2-2-1 and 2-1-2 layout. Cramped 5 seats in a row where everyone else in their aircraft class has 4 seats! Seats are narrow, uncomfortable and the couple's seat by the window lack ANY work space area and minimal storage. The dining tray is a primitive design of a pullout from the small divider between the seats. The shoulder belt cuts right into your neck as 2 FA's admitted to this defective design! There is zero privacy on the isle seats.

I flew from LAX to Zurich and back to LAX with Swiss airlines. On both flights the seats were so narrow that when I saw my middle seat on the outbound flight I was thinking whether I'll fit in that space. And I'm not a big guy by any means (5':10" = 178cm tall, 155lb=70Kg). On the return flight I paid 44Euros and got an isle seat but when I boarded I saw an overweight lady sitting in the adjacent seat and the arm-rest was not coming down! Thanks got her husband was elsewhere and we changed seats. The overhead luggage space is so narrow that you should put your carry-on sideways. Their planes are not really suitable for long distances.  As for the on-flight entertainment system, It was showing advertisements and you where not given option to watch a movie or something until one hour into flight. Their food and beverage service was OK like any other reasonable airline.

Swiss reminds me of a budget airline, similar to the European low cost carriers. Very narrow seats with very little leg space, maybe 28-29 inches. If you are over 6 feet tall, good luck. Every US domestic airline provides more leg space than our friends from Switzerland. A 3-4-3 seat configuration on a Boeing 777 says it all. I will definitely avoid them for international travel.

On both my Boeing 777 and Airbus Swiss Air flights, the seats in front of me reclined so far the entertainment screen was inches from my face. It was extremely claustrophobic and uncomfortable. I've flown on at least a dozen airlines and have never seen seats recline so far. I loved everything else about the airline but would not fly them again for this reason alone. I'm short so I can't imagine how bad it is for tall people.

Cramped into an A330-300 economy seat. Knees were pressed hard into the seat row in front of me. Seat row pair in front of me was installed crooked (as in improperly). When the passengers in front of us reclined fully, the IFE screen was 6” from my face and the headphone jacks didn’t work. Armrests didn’t go up, so in an emergency, I could have been trapped as there was no room to get out of the seat unless I woke up the passenger in front of me and made them put their seat up. Hands down the worst trans-Atlantic crossing I’ve ever made. Avoid this airline.

Absolutely disgusting flight with TAP Portugal business class from Warsaw to Lisbon. They put a charter plane rented from Get Jet which is a low cost airline experience. The seat even in the front row (business class) is extremely cramped with no legroom whatsoever. Seats are very uncomfortable and just not worthy of any business class fare.

I like to check seat maps and reviews before booking my flights. In case of my Toronto to Lisbon flight with TAP Portugal, I was unable to find any seat reviews online for this aircraft. I paid a significant premium to select 12F, an exit row window seat. This was an overnight flight, so I thought this would be a good opportunity to sleep. Unfortunately, the seat was extremely narrow, hard, width-restricted by those fixed armrests that you typically only see at bulkhead seats and also missing an armrest on the fuselage side. Also, it was surprising that the person in 11F was able to recline their seat. Exit Rows are not supposed to be able to be reclined into. There was also a very cold draft coming from the fuselage. The seat was so uncomfortable, that I spent the last 2 hours of the flight sitting on the floor and using my winter jacket to cover myself. Granted this was only possible because I had the exit-row legroom. In summary, selecting an exit row window seat on a a Tap Portugal A321Neo-LR is not wise and it is definitely not worth the premium price-tag they place on it.

Seat 6C, Boeing 787 Dreamliner. Scoot advertises this seat as having additional legroom, this is not the case. At this time I would not recommend that anybody does a seat upgrade on this airline. As far as I am concerned, the seats are getting smaller and smaller, with less and less padding. It's even difficult to reach to your seat belt to strap in. In regards to the inbuilt tray / table, very difficult to use if you are above average height.

I chose one of the Scoot Stretch seats, Row 1, seat C. I can highly recommend. This seat gave me the benefit not only of extra leg room, but also it was very quiet being far away from the engines. As well as this, I was one of the first on, and first off of the flight. Ample room for my 6'3" frame. I would say though, that the seat could probably use a little extra padding on the bottom part. I have worked in aviation, and I know that all the time airlines are trying to cut down on aircraft weight so the flight is more economical. But please Scoot, don't do it at the price of the comfort of your customers. Flight was only three hours long. I was starting to get a little uncomfortable by then. I could have gone perhaps another two hours maximum. Despite this, this is a good seat and I can highly recommend.

Economy Seats are terrible, if person is reclined you can’t get out, the seats are not comfortable. Customer service English is not good. I cant make my flight because the connection is late,  so my new flight the next day will be at 2030 when they mean 1230 is a problem. I was told i would not be reimbursed since my flight the next day was early. Wont fly on this airline again.

I would say I got given the worst seat on the plane even though there were other places available. Unusually for Tway meals and water was provided. However I found their service to still be most inadequate. The meal was just one box. The seat was supposed to come with a USB however just before take off the pilot said no USB was working. It would have been nice if they at least had the route map on display on one main screen for all passengers. What I also found displeasing is that though T'way is a no tv airline, they still had tv units installed. To make matters worse they still left the IFE control boxes installed. These were poorly located in the footwell area and took up half the space. Another awful feature of this flight was the underseat ambient lighting used when the main cabin lighting was dimmed. For some reason only my seat had a bright blue light under it which made it difficult to rest if my face had been angled downwards.

The seat was excellent. It's a bit old and the tray table shows its age, but given the fact it's old, it's the old-school type of leather seats. It's very wide and comfortable to take a nap. The seat and cabin in general was very clean and the crew sanitized my tray table when they served me my snack, so the seat was very clean. I would agree that TAR needs to refurbish their cabins but as of now, they're very good anyway.
Poor Economy class seating. Very small, no legroom and soft back seats, so you can feel passengers kicking you during the flight. No entertainment systems.
Very comfortable seating with plenty of legroom. Easy to move around the cabin. Meal was very nice too. Cabin staff very friendly and accommodating I would definitely recommend Thai Smile.
Cabin layout was great, cabin was beautiful and the seats were great good legroom and wider seats than usual in a 3-3-3 seat configuration also a lot more space

Aircraft was Thai's new B77-300ER. Seat layout is 3x3x3 and seem to be wider than other aircraft with 3x4x3 layout. Seat width seems OK because my shoulders were not bumping on to the person next to me (I was on an aisle seat). Seat pitch is fine at the start (I am 5'2") until the passenger in front of you recline their seat -- then your seat becomes uncomfortable and it becomes difficult to move your legs. Aisle space seems to be the same as other aircraft. Because there were fewer economy seats, thus fewer economy passengers, than in a 3x4x3 aircraft, we did not have to queue most of the time to use the toilets.

Because of the flu season there're not so many passengers so it felt very spacious. A bonus point for the crew was that they knew about this and try to separate individual passengers far away from each other to get more comfort. Seat can be reclined quite easy, no major technical fault. IFE is quite up-to-date with basic movies package and also game. Though in some seats the IFE may not work.

Other than the fact that there is almost no leg room and seat recline is minimum, my biggest complaint is the seat itself. Specifically, the seat cushion, which was beyond uncomfortable. The seat cushion had been compressed /crushed to a point where you either have to sit in a slouched position or you have to sit on a bump near the back of the cushion. This is not the first time I have encountered this problem on a Sunwing plane. Come on Sunwing, either invest in better seats, or change the cushions regularly.

Currently sitting on my flight from Colombo to Dubai and I'm shocked at how uncomfortable the economy class seats are. The middle of the seat has a big metal lump protruding out of it and when you lift the headrest, your shoulders are resting on more hard metal. The actual shape of the seats are awful too. They're almost curved so you feel like you're sitting like this: C. Not to mention the seats are thread bare with little to no cushion on them. The only thing I'm grateful for is the fact my flight is only 4.5hrs long, I don't know how I'd be able to cope with any longer. If you're considering Sri Lankan for a long-haul flight in economy and comfort is important for you, I'd strongly suggest you look elsewhere.
No room whatsoever - paid extra for it! Seats in row 4 have less legroom than rows 2&3 but cost the same. They were sold as "comfort" seats but this was very misleading.
Never again, hardly any legroom, seats were worn out, uncomfortable and almost no cushioning left. Hardly any storage in the seat pocket as they store lots of pointless magazines etc in there

The seat on the TUI Boeing 787-9 is very good after using 4 times long and short haul, I flew 9:30 to Jamaica in 2019 and the seat did get a bit cramped but that’s expected really after that time. The TV is acceptable but is not the biggest but does the job with an acceptable amount of content. The recline was pretty average. Overall the TUI Economy 787 seat was just above average quality and works great

Flight TOM136/137 to Phuket, Sound steady flight without turbulence etc, flight attendants good with free drinks and average food etc and clean cabin. 1 toilet in economy without light return flight. First time we have used Tui for long haul to Phuket, we have usually traveled to Bangkok with other carriers. So with regard to the seating, we were in seats 17a & 17b outbound and 20a & 20b inbound which is adjacent to the wing both ways. Found the seat structure ok, but the leg room compromised with the seat in fronts leg restricting space in what was a restricted leg room seat at best. Both seats were not what we expected for a long haul flight, more like the crampness you experience on short haul and quite poor at best. So all things considered would use alternative carriers as before and go via Bangkok and arrive more refreshed. With regard to the Boeing 787 extra measures to promote less jetlag ie mood lighting and more air etc, found this ineffective and couldn't sleep due to the crampness of the seat, so Dream on Tui.
Seat 13D is for me one of the best seat for this type of aircraft with legroom. You just have to accept the instructions to be followed for emergency exits.

Absolutely ridiculous leg room. I'm fairly tall, but have never encountered this on an intercontinental flight of 9 hours. This was pure torture. If I wasn't sitting next to the isle (which was also shockingly narrow, by the way!), I simply wouldn't have been able to sit, period. I could not move whatsoever and was in pain after a while. This is totally unacceptable and needs to be dealt with TUIfly! Never again.

On long haul flight Istanbul-Jakarta (and back) seats were quite narrow. I saw seat features map with 3x3x3 layout in the last aircraft compartment, in reality the middle section has four seats, so 3x4x3. Pitch is not good either, and not suitable for long haul flight. Everything felt squashed. The recline was okay-ish. The seat padding felt comfortable though, but this is not enough to make up for shortcomings re the seat width and pitch.
Horrible seats. Very narrow you can barely fit into it, and the leg room was awful. The headrests couldn't be moved, and the seat kept reclining because it wasn't working. Very uncomfortable.

Terrible seat configuration, very old and inconvenient, lack of privacy. Seat uncomfortable, little controls for various seating and sleeping configurations. Lie flat seat malfunctioned and could not lie flat during the flight. Could not change to other business class seats as they were all occupied. The airline did not offer any partial refund, only future flight discounts of 15%. Terrible customer services. Will never fly on Turkish Airlines again. Many other better choices.

We flew TK62 from IST to KUL in seats 3E/3F. Upon arrival, we saw industrial tapes on the middle divider between the seats. The tapes hardly hold the divider down and we in the end have to use a blanket in the middle slot to keep it down throughout the flight. No crew acknowledgement or apologies for such inconvenience.

Awful seats on the A330. Very uncomfortable legroom for a long haul flight from Istanbul to Bangkok. This had to be similar to a low cost airline's legroom and is not in the same league with any other airline. Utterly disappointed with this airline and I've had several bad experiences with Turkish Airlines a few years ago. Terrible legroom, seats were uncomfortable and dated (over 10 years the cabin is and starting to show its age) I will no longer fly Turkish Airlines for long haul and would be better off flying on 5 star airlines for long haul travels like Singapore Airlines, ANA, and Qatar Airways in the future.

I flew Turkish Airlines Business Class on a Boeing 773 from IST-LHR (Aircraft: TC-JJS). The cabin was clean. And the seat was also clean. Storage places were available under the foot rest area, as well as the storage bins and on the side of the seat below the reclining controls. Power supply was available under the arm rest. Wireless headphones were also provided. The IFE was controlled through a remote which was conveniently placed under the seat compartment, It was responsive with minimal lagging considering this was a slightly older cabin. The seat itself was very wide and comfortable. And it reclined into a full bed. However this was a day flight. I had reclined into a rest position but not a bedtime one.  The only thing the aircraft lacked was a privacy screen which I would prefer on longer hauls.. An excellent experience, I would definitely fly it again

When reserving the ticket, I have paid for seat selection and selected window seat (7A) for 12€ surcharge. There was no window in that row on that side of the plane. And as the plane was fully booked, I couldn’t change my seat after boarding it. The lack of the window in the seventh row was never mentioned during the reservation process, nor it was on the drawing during the seat selection.

My family and me were on our way back from 11 day holiday in Turkey, where we've been given 10a-c and 11a-b seats on boarding. Later we learnt those are emergency seats. When airplane started taxiing, crew chief came to my 16 yrs son seating on 10a and told he must leave that place because airline rules. He was separated from the rest of the family to the rear seats. Flight attendant told I can join him after the takeoff, but other attendant didn't allow that. I sent the complaint feedback asking why my son was separated from us, while my 15yrs daughter kept sitting on 11a - emergency exit. I asked why they issued us those boarding passes if that's against security rules? Did the airlines expose my daughter's and other passengers' lives to danger, because they didn't move her to other seat? I tried twice to get the answer, but they're obviously not reading the feedback carefully. They answered only to the reason why my son is displaced, not the other questions. It's very disappointing and will try to avoid THY as much as I can, since they not trying even to give serious explanation or apology.

I paid for an economy plus seat and what I got was the exact same uncomfortable seat for all of economy and maybe 2 inches more leg room. This is a scam by the airlines to make money and sell a product that is not worth the money.

The seats had less recline than ANA - which we flew coming to San Francisco airport. United Airlines is not the worst, but I can hardly recommend it. If there was any other option to fly into las vegas, I would take that instead.

United's Economy Class seating may be tight, and it can be challenging for someone taller than me. But the inflight entertainment is terrific, and the power supply is a mixture of plugs and USB ports.

United has audacity to call their product "First Class". I tried to sit in seat 4E on my flight yesterday from ABQ-SFO. The seats were old and dingy looking. The lumbar support was sticking out into my back like a rock. The button to control it was broken. I basically had to lean forward the entire flight. I will do my best to never fly United again. A truly garbage seat from an airline that obviously doesn't care.

Absolutely do not sit in row 15 (directly in front of exit row). The seats will not recline, but the row in front of you does, so you're left with maybe 12 inches between your face and the seat in front of you. Also the seat is so upright it feels like it's trying to push you out. I've flown on a few United flights for this business trip and I am not impressed with the seat comfort, layout, or timeliness of the airline in general. Of the 7 flights this week, all but 1 has been late departure/arrival.

My husband and I booked United from our trip back from Saudi Arabia. It was from Chicago to Minneapolis. They put us in two different seats. My husband asked the crew member to put us together. She was super rude and said now, he needs to sit where his seat is at. He said ok I will just wait for the person who’s placed next to my wife and I will ask to switch the seat. She replied no while rising her voice at him. She told him to seat where he’s scheduled to be. The person who was scheduled to seat next to my husband agreed to switch with us. We thanked him and I got to seat next to my husband. She came to the guy and was like sir you didn’t have to do, but I will give you points on your mileage or whatever she was talking about. Through out the trip which was 1 hr and 4 minutes to MSP she was loud and rude to us. We will never use United ever again.

I have been traveling for united airlines for many times, but they always have the most horrible service. Their customer service is very rude. I think that they very soon expect that the people pay for their services helping the people. I asked them about another seat because I am very tall and their answer was if you need to change your seat have to pay but in the middle.
Cramped seat in so-called Polaris class. No room for legs with seat fully extended. Worst business class seat ever. United should just rip out these seats and start over again.

The first class seat 4A is OK. The seat recline comfort and armresting is average. It's spacious enough, and fairly comfortable. However, the leg for say someone taller might be an issue with knee room restrictions. I'm 5'10. Especially, if the person forward of you reclines all of the way without any considerations. Bear in mind though that the row behind you is an economy one. There is NO physical bulkhead separation on these aircraft. Sometimes you'll get someone with happy feet kicking your seat. I hate this inconsiderate behavior. Knowingly or not. The direct overhead space (left aircraft seats with "A" designation. i.e. 1A, 2A, 3A, etc...) is for very small items. Like a coat or jacket. The overhead space in say seat 4B, you can fit a pretty good sized regulation carry on like a 22x14x8" or a good size back pack NO problems. All in all, the EMB 170/175/190's is a much more comfortable aircraft than say the older, very cramped ERJ135/145 regional jets.
Boeing 767-400 seat was new and comfortable. A lot of place (I'm oversize). The inflight fun system was new, and movie offer was on a high level.
On Thai VietJet flight VZ962 from BKK to DAD Seat 6A on an A320-214, the tray table was broken and unfortunately, the passenger in front decided to recline their seat.
My seat is 25D, near the walk-way, the footrest is narrow, no screen in front of the seat and it is upholstered with leather and I don't like it. It's just okay.

The A321-NEO is one of Vistara's newer planes and has 12 lie-flat seats in business class. While only on a 2-hour flight, I tried out the bed and it had enough space for me (6'3). A decent meal was provided on a single tray (flight during COVID). The seat provided enough privacy considering this was a domestic business class flight that typically has standard recliner seats. The IFE screen was large, bright and responsive. In addition to the IFE screen, there were power sockets present but were not very convenient to use.

I was pleasantly surprised with a lie flat business class seat for a less than 2 hour flight from Delhi to Mumbai. The seat was very comfortable with lot of storage, generous recline and ample leg room. It is slightly angled away to offer additional privacy. The IFE screen was quite large and easy to control with a touch screen controller. Charging slots are a bit only placed when you are seated but easily accessible when the seat is in lie-flat or recline mode. I used the lie-flat mode after breakfast and found it quite comfortable for a 6 foot adult passenger and could take a restful nap. Unsure about how comfortable this would be for long-haul but for medium-haul business this is a very comfortable seat.
I traveled in their A320 premium economy. Leg space, seat width are far better than standard economy class. Seats were clean.

Very poor seats that are too close together with 30" claimed pitch seemingly a dream.  I am 6'1" (185cm ) tall and could not sit straight. Seats at the window e.g. 9A/ 14A etc. are even worse. My knees and behind were very sore after both flights of 4.5 -5.5 hrs. each. No chance to rest or sleep too uncomfortable made worse by the fact that both flights were virtually full. Food is poor and expensive with only water and tea/coffee free. Staff were friendly and good Flights left on time ands were trouble free - but those seats! Do not fly Virgin Economy if you are tall

Virgin is back to a cheap low cost carrier offering like it used to be when it was Virgin blue. Uncomfortable seats where you can feel the rear passenger’s knee poking in your seat - buy your own food and drink except one free glass of water - NO usb or charging port, no entertainment you have to bring your own device to connect to their wifi entertainment, but no charging port?

The seat was okay, it was kind of dirty in the side cracks! and my tv remote was stuck. They provided water in the cup holder of the seat which was nice. The seat was pretty soft, so it is good for sleeping.

Horrible 4.5 hours of travel. The economy seats have zero leg room. There was no in flight entertainment for such a long flight. First round of snacks was offered by purchase only. Then the cabin crew came with another round of complimentary snacks. But people had already bought stuff on the first round. Economy class seats are horrible. There is not room to move your leg or even recline the seat a little bit. I would definitely avoid travelling in West jet because I cannot afford anything more that Economy class and their seats are just horrible.

We flew transatlantic from London (LGW) in October 2024. Upgraded to econoflex seats thinking it would be similar to economy plus on Air Canada with more space in the seat. The seats we got were no better than all the other economy seats and they were the most cramped and uncomfortable seats I have ever experienced; minimal padding and very narrow. So tight was the legroom, I could not physically reach down to the floor to retrieve items I dropped - i am not a large person at 5’ 7” and 160lbs. We booked three seats for three people but found there was no window in our row (9) on the left (port) side of the aircraft. It was not possible to read a magazine horizontally in front of me, it was propped up by the seat back in front of me. The seat pockets are fitted with inflexible netting which does not allow much to be stored; I had trouble getting my water bottle into the net. There are no screens in the rear of the seats; passengers must use their own devices to access the entertainment system which was not as extensive as other airlines provide. It was rudimentary and holding a phone or iPad up for the duration of the flight was a chore. The flight information was also pretty basic. WestJet have opted for only two toilets at each end of the aircraft, one for the economy cabin and another for business class. Not nearly enough for the number of passengers aboard since economy pax are asked not to use the business class bathrooms when the tiny curtain is across the aisle. I feel sorry for the cabin crew who have to work in extremely tight spaces. I think there was more space in the overhead bins than was provided for passengers. Finally, the overhead air nozzles were pathetic and provided a weak airstream despite our best efforts to adjust them while at the same time the aircraft interior was too warm for the entire flight.

This is undoubtedly the most uncomfortable airline seating we have ever endured. WestJet is obviously the Canadian version of Spirit Airlines here. The seats are too narrow, do not recline more than an inch, and there is no padding whatsoever. Worse than sitting in a lawn chair for five hours. I will do everything in my power to avoid this airline for the remainder of my natural days. Awful experience and never again.

Most uncomfortable seat I have ever been in, especially since it was a 5 hour flight. Absolutely no leg room, poor recline on seats, hard uncomfortable, narrow seats. The pilot and staff did a great job but this is a review of the plane not the staff.

Whilst the leg room on the outbound flight to Calgary seemed adequate, the width of the seating wasn't. I was unable to use both arms to eat. Neither the persons either side of me were big, in fact they were both small ladies. Whilst the seating was ok for short internal flights the width of the seating is not adequate for long haul. I would not travel with this airline again.

The seats are clean. They can be reclined a few degrees. Seat width is standard and ok for a normal sized person. The distance to the front seat is just long enough to not touch it although one has to sit completely straight. For a budget airline, the cabin feels rather roomy and doesn’t make one feel claustrophobic like in other airlines.
Extremely cramped, seats were very thin and had no padding. Very little room for my feet under the seat in front as well. Made worse when seat in front was reclined. Food choice was very poor
Seat were pretty comfortable, adjustable head part. the blanket on the seats were also comfortable. seats are wider because of the 2X4X2 composition.

Travelled business class in from LON to BLR on 28th oct and absolutely worst experience on business class. Small and cramped seats, less space and weird sitting arrangement., had to turn my head almost 180 degree to see outside window while seating on the window seat. Virgin Atlantic had the worst business class experience. I could literally peep in my front and back seats, no privacy at all.

We booked business class for our flight to and from New York. We fly business class a lot with other airlines but this is our first experience with Virgin Atlantic. While the service by crew was on par, the layout and space was awful. First, there is less storage room overhead than any international flight I have been on, let alone in business class. There is no room for any personal item such as laptop bag storage - even in coach there is underwear storage space. The lay flat beds fold over which feels like a waste of space and requires passengers to get up and adjust. All the seats face each other across the aisle, which is weird for privacy. In short, stop trying to cram so many seats into business class. Charge more if you need to but make it decent. Not flying Virgin business class again and will actively tell others not to unless things have changed.

Awful service. No food choices, no welcome drinks, no menus and poor quality overall. Can't believe how bad the service has slipped and COVID can't be blamed for this issue. This is budget cutting at its worse, while still charging premium prices to passengers. We paid £600 to upgrade to premium from economy and it was the worst decision ever. Upper class were given everything from champagne to snacks to meal choices and the rest of the flight had to mop up the scraps. Not the fault of the crew as half the stock wasn't loaded by ground staff, and they were in the line of fire from several passengers. Felt bad for them but they said that this was a regular occurrence that they don't have the stock or items to give a top service. Come on virgin, get your act together and up your game - there are several other airlines to choose from and customers will go elsewhere for better service.

The seat width is acceptable but has limited storage space. It turns into a flat bed but it won’t recline the way airline seats do. Virgin supplies a mattress and a blankets, as well as a pillow for each seat. Operating the seat is reasonably user friendly and has ample privacy but this is not an enclosed suite. USB and electric outlets are provided. The screen size was large but you can’t watch it if stowed. They wanted you to stow the screen during take-off and landing but you can’t watch those safety videos from that angle. I am surprised how this design was approved. The entertainment videos are plenty to keep you busy in the sky and you can have WiFi as well although you have to pay extra. Overall experience was good.

Virgin Atlantic service was exceptional but the seats layout was awkward. There was simply no privacy but I would admit the seat was very comfortable. This particular B787 seats are complicated to operate and simply not practical. USB power was not working. Food service was good although with a limited menu. Flight attendants were always there with professional service. The H lounge at LHR is also one of the best.

During this pandemic - I actually travelled Virgin Atlantic on the first trip after lockdown here in the UK that they had with passengers. Hiccups on the way were expected. The seat was wonderful, the leather is really soft and the crew are just brilliant. I had a bulkhead seat on 21A and there was plenty of legroom. Cabin Crew bring through these items that you can put your foot on, like a leg rest but it is moveable due to the bulkhead. My only downside would be that the screen is on the side of you and can get stuck when you try to stow it back to its original position.

Visibly uncleaned and undisinfected lounge after the previous flight! Old, almost worn out and visibly not regularly cleaned upholstery on the seats. Narrow and uncomfortable. Видимо непочистен и недезинфекциран салон след предишния полет. Стара, почти захабена и видимо непочиствана редовно тапицерия на седалките! Тесни и неудобни.

I had a window seat 15A. The seat cushion was rucked so it was impossible to sit comfortably. The window curves inward which seems to reduce further the limited knee room. SI still would recommend the airline as others who are under 5'8 won't be aggravated, and the seat cushion issue was presumably a rare occurrence?

XXL seat with extra-legroom situated at emergency exit (rows 12 and 13). Non-reclining. The extra space is good for tall people. The seat can be reserved either for a fee or as part of a package (privilege pass) valid for one year on all Wizz flights. It is also possible to pay directly to the cabin crew if seat is still available (the fee is € 20 if paid in the aircraft).

Rows 12 and 13 - emergency exit, more space. Slim chairs, not reclining, more comfort due to large space between the rows. Extra payment is needed (€ 20-40, depending on flight) or frequent flyer pass (€ 249 year, with other benefits included - priority boarding and large cabin bag).

I didn't expect much from a low-fare flight but the seats were bad even in those standards. We're talking about stiff seats, where one can feel the plywood underneath one's behind. No reclining, no neck support, and nothing but the bare necessities to allow you to strap yourself in and pray for the flight to end.

The seat was a bit narrow albeit well padded. The legroom was a bit cramped maybe because I had a large backpack with me, the legroom would have been better otherwise. The seat didn't recline, the seat table was sturdy although it would be better if it was a bit bigger. The seat is perfectly good for a two hour flight and it is a quite comfortable seat.
The seat wasn't really that comfortable. The seat wasn't reclineable. The legroom wasn't that great either but it was OK for an hour long flight. The seat storage was quite bad.
The seat was quite comfortable. There wasn't much legroom but it was ok. The seat did not recline at all, there aren't any buttons or anything to make it recline which is quite a big dissapointment.

Seat is perfectly spacious for an average height person (I am 5'5") and width is good too. Very clean cabin and i enjoy the aesthetic and colour of the cabin as well. Overall very nice especially for the price and it’s a budget airline

Non existing leg room at all I am 6.2inches tall it was plain and simple torture you think that if you paid premium seats you will have leg room not at all plus you have to pay for everything. I will not fly ever again in this Airline. Also the seat won’t recline at all. Horrible, this is ok only for kids and people less than 5 ft tall.
Really bad legroom, even for a budget airline. My knees were being crushed against the seat in front of me and the tray table made it even worse. It was an agonizing 3 hour flight.

I flew the lie flat seat from Narita to LAX on their Boeing 787. The check in was fast. I had prepaid for the checked in luggage as well as the meals on board. The lie flat seat was very comfortable. In fact, it was more comfortable than some business class lie flat seats. The free WiFi on board was virtually non existent. But that was ok since i downloaded some movies from Netflix prior to boarding. The plane was clean and modern. No complaints there. I was able to order water and snacks from my iphone. The prices were reasonable for snacks, meals and beverages. For lie flat seats, this was a bargain. The airfare was almost one third the cost of flying business class on other airlines. It was a very good value for the money. I would definitely fly Zip Air again to go to Japan.

Business class is just economy with an empty seat in the middle. At 188 cm tall, my knees hit the seat in front of me. When the passenger in front reclines the seat, it digs into my knees. And the flight is four hours. I don't recommend flying business class on this airline.

Horrible seat. No storage space beneath seat or overhead because another passenger put their bag up there. Very small labels to identify which is the correct seat and the cabin crew don't bother to give directions. No legroom, power sockets or entertainment. Wobbly tray table. Armrest was sticky and seat had droplets on it. At least I wore dark clothing to hide it rubbing off.

This review is for Warsaw to Chicago, Sept 5, 2023. Also, this is our first, and most likely last time we will fly on LOT. Positives: Very attentive and kind cabin crew. Plenty of beverages throughout the flight. Meals were somewhat basic (dinner and 'breakfast'), but adequate. Negatives: Very, very cramped. Not much space between rows, and even less when person in front of you reclines their seat. Given how little room there is, it is understandable that someone may want more space, but then there is no room to use your seat table. My wife had a drink on hers, which spilled when the person in front of her reclined their seat. If you drop something, good luck trying to find it while inflight. Aisles very narrow, barely any room to walk. For a 10+ hour flight, this is not a good choice.

In addition to the Long Haul and Untra Long Haul versions, Singapore Airlines operates a medium hall version of the A350 and that is by far my favourite. It offers the choice of either a left- or right-hand side consol. The seat configuration is 1-2-1 staggered. Each offers direct aisle access but for single seats with extra privacy choose A or K - 12, 15, 17, or 20. What makes these seats so great is they can be converted from upright to fully flatbed (and everything in between) with the push of a button. Unlike the other A350’s and 777’s with the crazy ‘flip’ seats that force you to sleep in a strange and uncomfortable angle. Regardless of where you sit, the seat offers a curved privacy wing with built in angle light options for reading. The 18″ screen provides access to the KrisWorld system which is loaded with movies, TV box seats, games and audio. You can control it by a touchscreen or use the remote which makes it easier to control the system while lying down. There is an AC power point and two high-speed USB charging ports in the console plus Business Class passengers can enjoy free Wi-Fi. There’s a blanket, large pillow, pair of slippers, eyeshades and a bottle of water at each seat. However, your unlikely to find an amenity kit, but these are available on demand.

We recently travelled Auckland - Singapore -London - Singapore - Auckland, on both the A350 and B777. Service was perfect, as usual, and food quality was generally good.Entertainment seems to have declined. The great disappointment was the Business Class seat, same on both aircraft. It cannot be fully reclined without conversion to a bed, and to put your feet up requires twisting diagonally into a barely comfortable position. Not much better when fully flat in bed form. I have travelled on Singapore business and first over almost 30 years, and this seat is the worst i have experienced.

Singapore Airlines have been updating their long-standing light-brown coloured economy seats with newer blue coloured seats. Whilst the inflight entertainment tech has certainly benefited, SQ have made a shocking choice of seat type / pitch. SQ state that these seats have a 32 inch pitch. I am definitely taller than average 6'8", but did fit in their previous economy seats. This is no longer the case. Whether it's due to the cushion thickness, design method of seat recline etc, the simple fact is that SQ's newer economy seats are far more cramped and uncomfortable. The SQ service remains good, but this doesn't really matter when you simply can't fit into their seats and experience genuine discomfort on long-haul flights. I experienced this issue on both their A350-900 and A380. In my opinion, when travelling long-haul, being in a seat with legroom and being comfortable, are the most important factors in choosing which airline to use next.

Like the majority of their regular business class passengers I hate the business class seats on their A380 aircraft. The seat and surrounding environment are great for take-off, landing or whenever in the normal seated position. But when it comes time to sleep, then good luck with that one. It soon becomes the most uncomfortable business class lay flat bed in the sky. What were they thinking? Well clearly, they were not.  At least they are more likely to get a decent night’s sleep that the poor passengers trying to get comfortable on this seat. Please Singapore Airlines – do something to address this issue. Given these aircraft are most likely going to be around for a lot longer that initially planned, don’t make your loyal customers continue to suffer. At least get some decent bedding.

A major fatal flaw in the terribly designed business class seat which is truly awful if you want to try to sleep! While it’s a flat bed you are forced to sleep diagonally with very narrow footwells so that if you want to change position to lie on your side then your other side it’s impossible! It’s to restrictive to move so you’ll hardly get any decent sleep unless you have consumed large amounts of alcohol from the great choice on the wine list - whoever designed this seat needs to be fired! Apparently talking to one flight attendant they did say there’s a refit of new seats & interior on this aircraft planned but wasn’t sure when. Seat adjustment controls worked if you hold & press, which is a bit outdated & needs improvement. lighting was sufficient for reading. Privacy on an aisle seat is never any good so if that’s what you want then window seat is recommended. So A380-800 business class seat not recommended & if you want a good nights sleep & opt for the A350 or 777 aircraft with Singapore.

We were in seats 33A and 33C - would highly recommend these seats as they are the last seats in premium economy section with a bulkhead behind which allows you to have the seat reclined whenever you like without interfering with passengers behind you. The first row seats in premium economy s 31 similarly have no seating in front as on exit row but TV screens are either mounted in between the seats in a centre console or on the bulkhead in front, excellent legroom but screen position could be an issue.

I had confirmed the seat suitable for my needs, had the seat confirmed with the boarding pass printed and issued to me. At the point of boarding I was told my seat was moved with no real reason given although we suspect it was to accommodate other passengers who do not seem to have any real reason to need to take over my seat. I ended up having to sit with the bad ear nearer to the aisle and could not hear what the flight attendant was saying. I am most displeased at this inconsiderate change without any prior discussion with me by the airline.

This seat is cramped. The pitch is 30-31 inches. The metal support from floor for seat in front is exactly in the space where you would naturally place your right leg, reducing the legroom significantly.
