I could not imagine siting in this seat for 12 hours, it would be torture. Luckily for me was a quick trip to Bangkok.

The most uncomfortable seat encountered. Minimal padding, no lumbar support, extremely uncomfortable, for the 6 hour flight to Cairns from Singapore. Don't book, unless you want to be in extreme discomfort, and have back ache for a day or two after. I am 6 ft tall, slim and fit. I booked an exit row seat thinking it would be more comfortable, but the seat has a stub as an arm rest meaning it is about 13 inches wide in practice.

I tried the new A388 business class from London to Singapore. It was about 12-13 hours. My seat was 21K on the upper deck, along with the suites (the old ones used to be in the bottom deck). I think that the seat was pretty spacious for me (I'm 164cm) the footrest was good, but the legroom was to either to your left or right, which makes it quite uncomfortable. But on the SQ regional J class, its a straight legroom, so consider getting a 787-10/359 if you want a straight legroom. The bed couldn't recline fully into a flat bed, unlike the 773,359, the 388 uses buttons to recline the bed, it is done automatically, while the 773/359 is done manually. The table was pretty small compared to the 773/359 (hard to get out of your seat while the table is open) and some tables are also not fully functional, like mine, during landing the table popped back out, I have tried several times to push the table back in, but it just won't fully go in, it would still be loose. The crew was very kind, friendly and welcoming. They kept checking on me, which made me feel weird but happy in a way. I had 2 meals in total on this flight, lunch and supper/dinner. The lunch wasn't my favourite, the scrambled eggs were pretty basic. But the Dinner/supper, I love it, it was steak beef served with mash potatoes and a couple of vegetables, (not book the cook).

Chose a window seat so I could lean against the pillow and window as I usually do. But due to large gap between seat and arm ready window side it was very uncomfortable. Leg room minimal. I’m 5,5 . It seems new but not well designed. Tray table not adjustable and too close to body.

Worst business class seat I’ve ever had. Very thin cushioning, not comfortable. Bed cover is not a mattress at all, just a thin piece of material. You can’t lie straight, you have to lie on an angle and rest your legs on the footrest with your feet in a small cavity. Very poor for a business class product, Avoid at all costs.

Not really comfortable chair or bed. Singapore Airlines offer a proper bed and a separate chair in First Suite: Both are rather disappointing, especially taken into account the huge investment and Publicity. The leather chair stands alone in the middle of the Suite, one has to move it from the take-off position, to the dining position, and to the outside view position. The bed is not facing the direction of travel, but crossways in the suite. The bed is narrow and very hard, not very comfortable. When the bed is not used, it hangs across the suite like a chunk of white painted wood. The whole design is not well thought through and not nicely done.

Worst business class seat I have experienced Automatic seat controls did not work on either the outbound or return flight, so flight attendant assistance was required several times. Same with the center wall divider partition that required attendant assistance to lock it in place for both flights. Seat design requires you to lie at an angle in order to use the foot rest space. Overall, was not impressed with this business class product &amp.

The 3x3x3 configuration on the A350-900 is desperately cramped. I have short legs but my knees were knocking against the seat in front and the 6 flights comprising my journey from London to Perth and return were spent with a neighbour's elbow poking into my side because of the narrowness of the seat and the armrest. Hard seats compounded the problem. No refresher towels or overnight comfort packs except a skimpy one on the outward leg on SA. Minimal food choice, and what was provided to me was inedible apart.
My seat (71J) was terrible. There was 2 black boxes fixed under the seat before me leaving me only 60% of the space that my feet would have had if I had been sitting in different row.

Seating is very uncomfortable.  Sleeping configuration is not comfortable. You need to sleep on an angle sticking your feet in a small hole. The seat is lightly padded. Food is low quality for business class and no longer offers a rich Peranakan mix, but a Chinese bias. Media system resets when any connected device detaches and reattaches. Book the chef food never got loaded.

Headrest is fixed and not changeable. Armrest are 2 small foldable tables.  IFE Flightinfo can not save changes to metric system by each change to movie or music an return to flight info. Touchbuttons to change the seat not working (crew needs to change the seat to bed). Bed is not to sleep for passengers who sleep on sides. Hole for feet is to small for footsize 46.

Boeing 787-10 leg room was adequate, it shouldn’t be a worry for medium-haul flights like this (SQ878). The screen size was good, it was difficult for you and your neighbor to see each other’s screens, giving you a decent amount of privacy. The 3-3-3 configuration makes it easy to access the aisles (with the exception of window seats) compared to most other wide body airliner. Power sockets are available to keep your devices charged. A cup holder is also present which was a nice touch as you no longer need to worry about your drink spilling over and onto your seat.

The Boeing 787-10 legroom is fine, but the seat feels very narrow and is uncomfortable. The A350 seats which I flew earlier were much better. Not sure if I would want to fly on Singapore Airlines Boeing 787 again.

We flew Singapore to LAX Premium Economy and were completely disappointed. The seats had recline and footrests alright but were so narrow we were both very uncomfortable all night. Food was awful (stale buns) Eg Pasta shrimp salad had no dressing, vegetables were stewed beyond recognition . Service was brusque to the point of being rude. Icecream tub was almost thrown at me in the haste to get service done quickly . No welcome drink. Requests for water were forgotten. We have in the past had the pleasure of travelling premium economy Air NZ and there is NO comparison. Don’t know what happened to Singapore Airlines supposed excellence for service. Their Premium Economy offering was fairly price competitive (albeit our first leg from Australia was only offered in economy), however I think they make this happen by essentially providing economy level meals (No amenities pack ). The poor service is a total shock. Have they lost their mojo?

This is the worst economy seating I have been on,  the seats are very narrow and the seating hard. Having the back upright feels like you are being pushed froward, in recline they are just about tolerable. The leg room is very tight that cannot move your feet. There is no arm room and if you are in an aisle seat you are constantly being knocked by passengers and crew as they pass. The earphone socket was broken i had an 8hr flight with no entertainment.

BA used a configuration of 2x3x2 seats per row. I was seated in a middle, small, claustrophobic cabin in the middle with no air flow. Service was handled over a passenger seating on both sides and stepping to the aisle required jumping over another passenger.

The business class of British Airways flying London to LA is very poor by comparison to other airlines, for the price. The seating is narrow, on top of a neighbor, no separate little cabin. It's also generally more expensive and the Avios are not worth collecting as there is rarely any availability.

Was sat on that famous row 35, seat 35H. Summary: 11.5 hours flight from LHR to GIG in seat that doesn't recline by default. The seats on the row 34 ahead recline, meaning it's a struggle for eating or drinking if passengers sat on row 34 keep their seats reclined. To make the disaster worse, the overhead bin compartment above rows 33 to 35 are occupied by cabin crew stuff. Means that it is extremely difficult to accommodate cabin luggage.

Recently flew BA’s nonstop between Boston and London on the A380. It is a massive airplane with a payload of over 500 passengers. Business class seating on this plane and on this route was not worth the $$ in my opinion. There were too many seats in each row making the seats narrower than those offered by other airlines. Most jumbo jets have a 1-2-1 configuration in business class; this plane had 2-3-2 and 2-4-2, twice as many seats in each row. This is particularly obnoxious if you are seated in the middle aisle because that means anyone seated in a window seat or in the middle seats has to crawl over an aisle passenger just to get to the bathroom and back. If you do so in the dark on an overnight flight, it is actually unsafe for you and that poor aisle passenger. Check the plane scheduled for the flight you want to take and if a 777 is offered, opt for that one. They are all equipped with Club Suites in Business now.

Sat in seats 24a outbound to Budapest and 18A return flight from Bucharest. Seats were both very worn and had a ridge running a couple of inches from the rear. My backside was numb on both flights and less than 3 hours for each flight. Legroom far to little for a national carrier. Also on the return flight the seat pocket had a hole at the bottom and only found this out when i put items in it and they fell on the floor and due to the lack of space had to ask fellow passengers if they could reach my stuff which they kindly did. USB charger  going very intermittent as well. I will avoid British Airways on short haul flights if possible.
One of the worst business class seats, tiny seat. The lay out of the aircraft is very cramped, the plane was very dirty, amenity kit awful, service in general, not so good.

BA doesn't seem to understand why its customers choose to fly with them over low-cost carriers like Ryanair, easyJet or Wizz Air and the keep racing to the bottom, despite never being cheap enough or comprehensive enough in terms of flights to certain destinations. They've installed the same appalling slimline seats easyJet and Wizz Air have, but managed to make them even more uncomfortable. They have no lumbar support, and also don't have headrests like BA's old Pinnacle seats. They also have no recline and despite being refurbished had no at seat charging either. My understanding was that seats upto row 12 should have the old Pinnacle seats, so I woke up early to check-in just as check-in opened on the app 24hrs before and was pleased to bag a seat in row 10 which should mean I have the old Pinnacle seat. Apparently not, at least not on BA Euroflyer their subsidiary at Gatwick, the whole plane had the new appalling slimline seats even in Business - I'd have been pretty appalled if I had paid extra to fly in that cabin and been left with that seat for 3hrs. They are probably ok for an 1 maybe 2hr flight max, but on a 3hr flight to Catania from Heathrow it was painful and we were left with a horrible back pain.

Boeing 787-9 - not worth the money. The seats were extremely narrow so like lying in a coffin. When the seats were out (which is all the time on these long flights) you have to clamber over passengers to get to the toilet. The configuration of the cabin means that some one is always waking up someone else. This is an economy seat masquerading as a business class seat and is misleading and deceptive conduct because there is NO WAY you can get any rest if you book with British Airways.
Worst seat we have ever had to endure on a long haul flight. No room at all and not what we expected would not recommend this airline

Did research, premium economy, looks good with extra width seats more legroom and extra recline on the seats. We had a 20 hour red eye flight LHR to SYD with a refuelling and quick crew change in SIN. Looks deceive. We were seated in row E (middle 2 of 4) centre aisle. Great, until the seat in front reclined and we discovered we were trapped. The seat arms are not retractable, (that is where the tray table is located). The distance between the arm rest and the fully reclined seat in front is under 7 inches. To extract yourself you have to wake 3 passengers, 2 in front to lift their seat backs to an upright position and the passenger to your side to allow you to lift your legs up over the arm rests. I found it impossible to watch my screen due to it being so far off vertical, it was sending me dizzy looking at it. One other problem I discovered, because I was stressed at being uncomfortable I started getting hot to find the Boeing 777 does not have individual air conditioning cold air nozzles, once the temperature is set it can’t be individually cooled. On the positive side the food was good I did however miss the coffee pot after the meal.

The most uncomfortable flight I have experienced due to the metal boxes under the seat in front. Outbound chose a window seat on lower deck and had one metal box under my seat that made sitting straight very difficult, so on way home opted for an upper deck seat in a set of two with my husband so I could at least get up and stretch. There was two boxes this time, and had pins and needles in my legs for not only the entire flight but for several hours afterwards. As vegan flyers we are never wowed with food, but this one was the worst yet, plain rice and vegetables.

Was sat in the emergency exit row. Ample leg room but was a little tight with elbow room. Entertainment system was ok but would prefer a newer movie selection. Breakfast meal was a little heavy, but enjoyed the selection including fruit, yogurt and croissant. Service professional and courteous. Overall the flight was enjoyable

The seat is quite comfortable and has good legroom, there is good space on the window seats, the IFE is outdated though and you can't adjust the angle of the head rest. The window is very big and your receive some sort of service every 1-2 hrs.

This flight was as I had experienced with all other BA flights I've had. The seats are comfortable, the bedding provided is pretty good, the food on-board (I always order an Asian Vegetarian Meal) was brilliant and the cabin crew brilliant. I sat on one of the window seats (rear-facing) and the privacy you get with the privacy divider up is pretty good. I always select the window seat on the last seat of the cabin (3A on this flight) to prevent having to step over someone else. The only possible criticism I can find for the set is the lack of storage space and how inconveniently placed the one storage bin is. BA is pretty good otherwise.

Was disappointed at first to see I was on the Boeing 777-200 but realised it was the updated club suite cabin so wasn't sad for long. The 1-2-1 configuration is a step up from their 2-3/4-2 configuration and the privacy on the seats is pretty good. The door isn't helpful and is more of a gimmick (could've been higher). The new IFE screens are way better than the older ones, they are more clear and bright and responsive than the old IFE screens. The seats on club suite are still fabric, which in my opinion, is better than leather and more comfortable. The seats now have convenient storage bins and power ports which is a very big improvement when compared to the old club world. The seats also have adjustable armrests which make sliding out of your seat during meal services easy. The service, in general, was fantastic and very similar to other BA flights I've had. All in all club suite is a pretty big improvement over the old business cabin.

All I ask is that BA increase the seat pitch by one inch - one inch would make such a difference; as would a little more padding in the seat and lumber/small of the back region of the seat on this Boeing 777-200.
